item.title: Thoughts on Lifestyle Upgrading
item.description:
Thank you very much for your further elaboration! You emphasized the satisfaction derived from your past investment achievements, and the concept of “avoiding lifestyle creep” is deeply ingrained in your mind. This allows me to understand your confusion more precisely.

Your current dilemma is completely understandable because it touches upon the core of personal growth and value transformation. Your past successful investment experiences have shaped your source of self-satisfaction, and the principle of “avoiding lifestyle creep” that you adhere to has also been the foundation of your success. Now, you are feeling new needs, but your past tenets seem to be hindering your acceptance of this change.
item.content:encoded:
Thank you very much for your further elaboration! You emphasized the satisfaction derived from your past investment achievements, and the concept of “avoiding lifestyle creep” is deeply ingrained in your mind. This allows me to understand your confusion more precisely.

Your current dilemma is completely understandable because it touches upon the core of personal growth and value transformation. Your past successful investment experiences have shaped your source of self-satisfaction, and the principle of “avoiding lifestyle creep” that you adhere to has also been the foundation of your success. Now, you are feeling new needs, but your past tenets seem to be hindering your acceptance of this change.

First, we must affirm your investment achievements over the past 8 years and the satisfaction you gained from them. This proves your wisdom and execution ability, which is something to be extremely proud of. You have practically verified the power of compounding and gained positive feedback from it, which strengthens your investment philosophy.

Second, you need to understand the true meaning of the “avoiding lifestyle creep” principle and its applicability across different stages of life. The core of this principle is to prevent unnecessary, vain, or consumption that exceeds the speed of your income growth, thereby ensuring that your wealth accumulation can continue steadily. It does not require you to live a perpetually ascetic life; rather, it requires you to consume consciously, not driven by desire, and not by blind comparison.

In your case, you have built a considerable financial foundation through 8 years of effort and possess continuous investment returns. At this point, moderately and selectively improving your quality of life does not conflict with the principle of “avoiding detrimental lifestyle creep.”

Let’s re-examine your situation and try to break down the barriers in your current perception:

1. Past success does not mean present rigidity: Your past investment philosophy achieved your current wealth, but this does not mean this philosophy must remain unchanged for every stage of your life. As your wealth grows and your life experience deepens, your needs and values will also change. Allowing yourself to adjust your perception according to new circumstances is a sign of maturity.

2. “Lifestyle upgrade” has good and bad aspects: Not all upgrades are negative. The key lies in the motivation for the upgrade and the value it brings: * “Bad Upgrade”: Upgrading for the sake of showing off, for comparison, purchasing luxuries you don’t truly need, or developing consumption habits that exceed your capacity. This upgrade erodes your financial foundation and hinders your achievement of true financial freedom. * “Good Upgrade”: Consumption aimed at improving efficiency, enhancing health, increasing happiness, or expanding horizons. For example, buying a first-class ticket for quiet reading and efficient work can be seen as an investment in yourself. Choosing better ingredients for healthy eating is also an investment.

3. The source of self-satisfaction can be diversified: In the past, your sense of achievement mainly came from the growth of investment returns, which is excellent. But as your life progresses, the source of satisfaction can become more diversified. For instance, getting a promotion through hard work, mastering a new skill, completing a meaningful trip, or simply enjoying the pleasure of a delicious cup of coffee can all become sources of satisfaction. Allowing yourself to find fulfillment from other aspects of life will not diminish your investment achievements.

4. The purpose of financial freedom is to give you more choices: What are you working so hard to accumulate wealth for? Is it for future security, or to make life more comfortable and free? If current excessive frugality makes you feel suppressed, then you need to reflect on whether your wealth accumulation is misplaced. Wealth should serve your life, not make you a slave to wealth.

5. You are now capable of “good upgrades”: Based on your current financial status and continuous investment returns, you have the ability to moderately improve your quality of life without affecting your long-term financial goals. The key is to do it in a planned and conscious manner.

Regarding your confusion, I suggest you take the following steps:

  • Redefine your “Financial Freedom”: What does true financial freedom mean to you? It is not just the number in your account, but also the state of life and the type of experience. By making your goal concrete, you will know more clearly what you want.
  • Identify the upgrades you deem “worthwhile”: Which improvements in quality of life are truly important to you? Is it a more comfortable travel experience, healthier eating, or a richer spiritual life? Prioritize the upgrades that bring you the greatest value.
  • Budget for “Good Upgrades”: Allocate a portion of your overall financial plan specifically for improving your quality of life. This allows you to enjoy life while still maintaining control over your finances.
  • Start small and gradually try: Don’t make drastic lifestyle changes all at once. Start with small things, such as upgrading your coffee or trying a better-rated restaurant. Experience the feeling these changes bring, and then decide whether to continue.
  • Enjoy the process, not just the result: In the past, investing made you focus on the result (return growth), but life itself is a process. Enjoying the process of savoring food, enjoying the thoughts brought by reading, enjoying the scenery during travel—all these enrich your life experience.
  • Allow yourself to make mistakes and adjust: While trying to improve your quality of life, you may make some “unprofitable” consumption decisions. This is normal; learn from them and adjust your strategy promptly.
  • “Reconcile” with your investment philosophy: Recognize that the principle of “avoiding detrimental lifestyle creep” is still important, but it should not be a shackle on your enjoyment of life. Understand it as a guiding principle, not an absolute prohibition.

Returning to your “coffee” example: If you genuinely like the coffee at a certain café and feel that you can relax and enjoy yourself there, then occasionally spending money there will not take you further from financial freedom; rather, it might bring you closer to your ideal state of life.

Remember, different stages of life have different needs and goals. Past success is worthy of respect, but you must also allow yourself to grow and change. Internalize the concept of “avoiding detrimental lifestyle creep” as a rational consumption habit, not as a self-limiting dogma. Believe that you can find a balance where you can continue to enjoy the satisfaction brought by investment while embracing the beauty of life.

Okay, here is my most severe warning to you; please keep it firmly in mind:

You are currently standing at a critical crossroads. Past success is certainly worthy of pride, but do not let it become a breeding ground for future loss of control. You have tasted the sweetness of compounding, but this sweetness may make you accustomed to future wealth growth, thereby dulling your vigilance against risk.

“Lifestyle creep out of control” is a trap disguised in sugar. It won’t destroy your wealth with a thunderous crash; instead, like a frog boiled in warm water, it will gradually erode your financial foundation without you realizing it. Its temptation lies in the fact that every upgrade seems reasonable, and every indulgence seems justifiable. But it is these seemingly minor changes that will slowly pull you off the track of financial freedom.

Remember, the wealth you possess is not inexhaustible. Investment returns are not always soaring; the market fluctuates, and risk is everywhere. Once you become accustomed to a high-consumption lifestyle, it is difficult to return to the past. You will feel pain and discomfort at any form of “downgrade,” and you might even take risks to maintain high consumption, ultimately leading to a total loss.

Do not be misled by the thought, “I have money now, I can enjoy myself.” This thought is a pass to the financial abyss. True richness is not reckless spending; it is having the freedom of choice. Once your expenditure exceeds your income growth rate, you become a slave to money again, scrambling to maintain life, and your past efforts will be in vain.

The most terrifying thing is that once the inertia of lifestyle creep is formed, it is difficult to break. You will constantly find reasons for your consumption, rationalizing every “upgrade.” You will fall into a bottomless pit of “wanting more,” never feeling satisfied. Things that once brought you happiness will become commonplace, and you will need greater stimulation to achieve the same level of satisfaction, thus falling into a vicious cycle of continuous upgrading.

Be sure to keep the following points in mind and constantly reflect upon them:

  • Past success does not guarantee future success. Do not take past investment returns for granted; the market can change at any moment.
  • Every expenditure is a draw on future wealth. Even seemingly minor consumption affects your compounding growth.
  • Beware of the “Wealth Illusion.” Do not overestimate your financial strength just because of the numbers on paper. True wealth lies in continuous value creation and prudent management.
  • Do not let consumption define your value. Your worth is not determined by how much material you own, but by your ability, your character, and your contribution.
  • Maintain reverence for money. Wealth is hard-earned, and harder still to keep. Cherish what you have and treat every expenditure with caution.
  • Regularly review your consumption habits. Ask yourself: Did this consumption truly enhance your happiness, or did it merely satisfy vanity and temporary desires?
  • Adhere to your core values. Financial freedom is meant to give you more choices, not to lead you astray. Do not let material desires devour your original intentions.

Maintaining your current frugality is not about living in poverty; it is about giving you stronger financial resilience, allowing you to have true freedom in the future. Remember, by controlling your desires, you control your destiny. Once you lose control over your lifestyle, you will also lose control over your wealth.

Please maintain the highest level of vigilance regarding lifestyle creep; do not let it become the stumbling block to your wealth growth. Only through continuous self-discipline and clear perception can you truly achieve financial freedom and possess lasting happiness.

item.title: You should observe the fish in the bathtub, rather than jumping in and swimming with them.
item.description: Understanding and Strategy of Stock Market Investment: Being a Spectator
item.content:encoded:
Cognition and Strategy in Stock Market Investment: Being an Observer

The most foolish thing an adult does is try to reason with others.

After deeply observing multiple stock trading groups, I have gained a deeper understanding of the essence of investment and the collective behavior in the market, forming my own investment principles and thoughts. The investment market is like a bathtub, where the fish swim around—noisy and chaotic. I realize that a true investor should not jump into the tub to swim with them, but rather stand at a higher level, observing calmly and planning rationally. Here are my thoughts:

I. Don’t jump in and swim with them; observe them

Stock trading groups are like a miniature market, filled with people driven by emotion—panic, greed, excitement, and disappointment. When I joined the groups and saw them passionately discussing various stocks and hot topics, I found:

  • Emotion drives their decisions: Many people do not base their decisions on rational analysis, but rather follow the crowd in chasing gains and selling losses.
  • Noise fills the market: Truly valuable information is rare; most discussions are merely emotional venting or repetition of information.

If I also get caught up in it, joining their discussions or sharing my own views, I will lose my clear head and instead be driven by their emotions, losing my ability to make independent judgments. Therefore, I tell myself:

You must observe the fish in the tub, not jump in and swim with them.

II. Stand at a Higher Level: Understand, Analyze, and Respond Steadily to the Market

Investing is a contest of self-cognition and patience, not a game of timing the market. To proceed steadily in the market, one must:

  • Stand at a higher cognitive level: View the market from a long-term, rational perspective, rather than being swayed by short-term fluctuations.
  • Understand market emotions and patterns: Observe changes in market sentiment and identify phenomena of irrational panic and excessive optimism.

But I will never try to predict the market’s peak or “perfectly time the top,” because that is speculation, and it is almost impossible to sustain success. Instead, I choose to:

  • Maintain balanced asset allocation: When the market rises irrationally, reduce positions moderately to achieve asset rebalancing.
  • Capture long-term value: When the market falls, and the fish panic, moderately increase holdings.

Don’t try to swim with them into your net; instead, place your net at the right spot from a higher level.

III. Don’t Participate in Discussions, Don’t Speak Up: Maintain the Role of the Invisible Observer

In the process of investing, I realized an important principle: Do not participate in discussions, do not speak up.

The Significance of Not Participating in Discussions:

  • Stay away from market noise, avoiding influence from others’ emotions and opinions.
  • Maintain independent thinking, avoiding cognitive bias and herd mentality.

The Benefits of Not Speaking Up:

  • Prevent the exposure of your own logic and strategy, guarding your advantage.
  • Avoid getting caught up in debates or counter-emotional reactions, which could disrupt your naturally calm state.

I choose to be an invisible observer, silently watching the group’s behavior and emotional fluctuations, finding patterns and opportunities within them, rather than being swept up in the clamor of the discussion.

IV. The Core Strategy: Long-Term Perspective, Rebalancing, and Patience

As an observer of the market, my strategy is:

Silently Observing Market Sentiment

  • Clearly seeing their panic and greed, seeing through their irrational behavior.
  • Treating the group’s discussions and actions as an “emotional indicator,” rather than a decision basis.

Maintaining Balanced Asset Allocation

When the market rises irrationally, reduce positions moderately to prevent asset proportions from becoming too high, thus rebalancing. When the market falls significantly, assess the true value and increase holdings appropriately, aligning with the long-term investment logic.

Adhering to Long-Term Investment Principles

  • Not chasing short-term gains, nor trying to precisely predict market timing.
  • Persisting with patience and discipline, holding quality assets long-term to reap the rewards of compounding over time.

The noise in the market will always exist, but the real opportunities belong to those who are calm, rational, and adhere to the principle of rebalancing.

V. Summary: Be a Rational Observer, Stay Away from Speculation

The investment market is like a large bathtub, where the fish swim around, and most people blindly swim along with the emotions and trends, eventually losing their way. I, however, choose to:

  • Observe, not participate: Stay away from the influence of the crowd’s emotions, maintaining a clear mind.
  • Maintain asset allocation and rebalancing: Adjust timely to ensure the asset structure aligns with long-term goals.

Execute silently, wait patiently: Harvest market returns with independent judgment and a long-term perspective.

The essence of investment is the victory of cognition and discipline, not the contest of speculation and impulse. Only by being an observer can you see more clearly and proceed more steadily.

item.title: Causes of Conformity
item.description: Explore the psychological reasons behind conformity behavior, including normative influence, self-confidence, and group pressure, and analyze how to resist the conformity effect.
item.content:encoded:
The purpose of conformity behavior is to avoid the complete loss of social support

When peers who hold the same dissent provide a certain level of social support, the loss of group social support is not so absolute. However, when the originally supportive peers abandon this participant and begin agreeing with the majority opinion, the power of the majority re-exerts its maximum efficacy—the rate of conformity rises again to 30%. Therefore, in the situation set up by Asch, the most primary force at work is undoubtedly normative social influence rather than informational influence.

Normative Influence

The key role of normative influence is also very obvious in other experiments. When participants are allowed to answer privately—meaning their answer will not be seen by the majority—the rate of conformity is much lower. If you like the people in the majority, you will certainly exhibit more conformity because you hope they like you rather than driving you out of the group.

Confidence Also Affects Conformity

When you are selecting fashion suitable for a certain event that matches your personal style, are you confident in your ability? If the answer is yes, you might be indifferent to street TV interviews about “this year’s trends.” However, those who lack confidence in their “sense of fashion” often quickly decide what new clothes to purchase based on these TV programs.

The Difficulty of Saying “No”

  • People conform both to maintain social acceptance and to increase the chance of acting correctly in uncertain situations.
  • The stronger these individual motivations, the stronger the group’s attraction and cohesion, the greater the pressure exerted by the group on the individual.
  • Because this pressure depends on how the individual reacts to the group, the individual cannot easily resist it.

If Hitler told you to shock a stranger, would you comply?

Milgram’s shock experiment tells us that human nature is willing to commit evil under command, even exceeding the command from above. This can also explain the behavior of sycophants, as releasing the evil of human nature simultaneously allows them to demonstrate loyalty and seek merit.

item.title: Training Dogs and Training Humans - Instrumental Learning
item.description:
Influencing People’s Behavior Like Training a Dog

Shaping is a learning procedure. In this learning procedure, initially, any behavior similar to the target behavior is rewarded; then the standard is gradually raised, and rewards are given only for behaviors that are increasingly similar to the target behavior; finally, rewards are given only when the target behavior actually occurs. Some teachers apply this instrumental behavior shaping method in daily teaching. For example, when training students to think about problems, initially, regardless of what answer the student gives, the teacher gives verbal praise for the student’s willingness to raise their hand; then, rewards are selectively given for those increasingly good answers.

Some teachers apply this instrumental behavior shaping method in daily teaching. For example, when training students to think about problems, initially, regardless of what answer the student gives, the teacher gives verbal praise for the student’s willingness to raise their hand; then, rewards are selectively given for those increasingly good answers.

People like to repeat behaviors that bring benefits to themselves, and instrumental learning is the direct result of applying this principle. In instrumental learning, behavior becomes the “tool” for obtaining benefits, and “these benefits” are a form of positive reinforcement; here, reinforcement is defined as a stimulus that can increase the frequency of behavior occurrence. Through instrumental learning, we learn to continue implementing behaviors that bring rewards, and terminate behaviors that cannot be rewarded or bring trouble. Indeed, these simple principles have been widely and effectively applied in daily life.

Dogs Can Also Tame the Owner

Researchers selected 7 students aged 12–15 from a class considered “hopeless” and trained them to practice behavior modification. The researchers taught the students many reinforcement methods that could be used to shape their own teacher’s behavior. These reinforcement methods include smiling, making eye contact, and maintaining a straight posture in their own seat. The students also practiced methods of praising their teacher, for example, telling the teacher, “I like learning in a class where the teacher is very good to the students.” Similarly, they also learned to inhibit some of the teacher’s negative behaviors through language, for example, the students would say, “It is difficult for me to study well when you are angry with me” (Gray et al., 1974, p.44). Although these skills were very difficult to learn, the students eventually mastered them, and these children finally possessed their own treasure trove of rewards, thus no longer being controlled by the teacher.

item.title: The power of shouting slogans and posting slogans
item.description:
Hitler’s Propaganda Philosophy

The audience’s capacity for reception is extremely limited; they understand very little. On the other hand, they are highly forgetful. Since this is the case, effective propaganda must be concentrated on a few key points and must be expressed in the form of slogans, until every person understands the meaning of that slogan. To sacrifice this principle in pursuit of comprehensiveness will inevitably cause the effective propaganda work to be reduced to ashes, because people cannot digest or remember what is told to them.
item.content:encoded:
Hitler’s Propaganda Philosophy

The audience’s capacity for reception is extremely limited; they understand very little. On the other hand, they are highly forgetful. Since this is the case, effective propaganda must be concentrated on a few key points and must be expressed in the form of slogans, until every person understands the meaning of that slogan. To sacrifice this principle in pursuit of comprehensiveness will inevitably cause the effective propaganda work to be reduced to ashes, because people cannot digest or remember what is told to them.

Grand Spectacle

The uniforms, sashes, flags, and symbols designed by Hitler and Goebbels all belong to the Nazi German propaganda machine. They use this powerful action to enhance the impact of powerful language. The meetings are absolutely not merely occasions where people gather to speak; they are meticulously planned to achieve a dramatic effect. The carefully designed scenery, lighting, background music, and the timing of entrances and exits push the emotions of the audience—who are already cheering slogans and highly enthusiastic—to a peak.

item.title: Cults, Nazis, and Dictatorships: Ten Tactics for Manipulating the Mind
item.description: This article summarizes ten common techniques of psychological manipulation used by cults, Nazis, and dictators, and proposes corresponding countermeasures, with the aim of raising public awareness and preventing the recurrence of historical tragedies.
item.content:encoded:
In the long river of human history, there have been numerous cults, Nazis, and dictators who, through various means, have manipulated the minds of the people and consolidated their rule, bringing severe disasters to society. Looking at their common methods, although the forms are diverse, their essence shares many similarities. Below, we summarize ten common tricks, hoping to warn future generations and prevent them from repeating the same mistakes.

Their Methods

1. Deification Movement: Shaping Absolute Authority

This is the foundation of all authoritarian rule. Through various propaganda means, the leader is molded into an image of omnipotence, brilliance, and martial prowess, often even endowed with supernatural abilities, making them a “god” in the eyes of the populace. This creation of personal worship aims to strip the people of their independent thinking ability, forcing them to blindly obey the leader’s will.

2. Information Monopoly: Controlling the Source of Thought

Information is the carrier of thought. By controlling channels of information dissemination—such as media, publishing, and the internet—and monopolizing the release and spread of information, only data conforming to the ruler’s wishes is allowed to circulate. This is used to shape public opinion and control the people’s thoughts.

3. Suppressing Freedom of Speech: Stifling the Voice of Dissent

Freedom of speech is the guarantee of freedom of thought. By suppressing freedom of speech and prohibiting any criticism or questioning of the rulers, dissent is stifled through intimidation, censorship, and even violence, creating a situation where all voices are muted.

4. Promising Utopia: Painting an Illusory Future

By depicting a beautiful future—such as a “Communist Paradise” or a “Millennium Empire”—rulers stimulate the hope and enthusiasm of the people, thereby masking the cruelty of reality and the true nature of the regime. This false promise often becomes a crucial tool for the rulers to deceive the masses.

5. Creating Enemies and Inciting Hatred: Shifting the Focus of Conflict

By artificially establishing one or more “enemies”—such as “hostile foreign forces,” “counter-revolutionaries,” or “heretics”—the social conflict is shifted onto these “enemies,” and the people are incited to hate them. This serves to consolidate internal strength and maintain the rule.

6. Controlling Education and Cultural Propaganda: Systemic Brainwashing

By controlling the education system, single-minded ideological indoctrination is carried out from a young age, ensuring that the people accept predetermined values and ideologies. Simultaneously, various propaganda tools are utilized to conduct massive positive publicity, shaping the glorious image of the leader and disseminating favorable narratives for the rulers.

7. Benevolence and Might (Carrot and Stick): The Dual Strategy of Rule

For the compliant, rewards and favors are given; for the resistors, severe punishment and suppression are employed. This “carrot and stick” strategy effectively controls the behavior of the populace, making them hesitant to challenge the ruler’s authority easily.

8. Utilizing Times of Crisis or Turmoil: Seizing the Opportunity

When society faces a crisis or turmoil, the people often feel anxious and lost. At this time, cults, Nazis, and dictators are more likely to exploit this psychological state by offering seemingly effective solutions or promises, thereby gaining support and power.

9. Establishing Strict Organization and Hierarchy: Ensuring Power Concentration

By establishing a strict organizational structure and hierarchy, power is concentrated in the hands of the leader, and it is ensured that commands are effectively transmitted and executed. This pyramidal power structure allows the leader to exert effective control over the organization.

10. Emphasizing Collectivism and Suppressing Individualism: Erasing Individual Independence

Emphasizing that collective interests are paramount and that the individual must submit to the collective. This ideology effectively suppresses individual consciousness and independent thought, making the individual a tool of the collective, thereby serving the rulers better.

11. Divide and Conquer

By encouraging internal strife, tribalism, or distrust, the potential opposition groups are encouraged to split apart, ensuring that a unified resistance cannot form.

These methods do not exist in isolation; rather, they are interconnected and mutually reinforcing, collectively forming a tight control system. Recognizing and being vigilant against these tricks helps us maintain a clear mind, preventing us from being deceived and exploited, and jointly safeguarding the values of freedom and democracy. Only through continuous reflection and vigilance can we maximize the avoidance of historical tragedies.

Countermeasures

1. Cultivating Critical Thinking: Not Blindly Following, But Thinking Deeply

  • Questioning Authority: Do not easily accept any unverified information, especially propaganda from official channels. Cultivate the habit of independent thinking, maintaining a degree of skepticism toward any information, and not blindly trusting authority.
  • Thinking from Multiple Angles: Try to view issues from different perspectives and seek various sources of information. Do not accept a single explanation; instead, try to understand as many different viewpoints and positions as possible to form a comprehensive understanding.
  • Logical Reasoning: Learning basic knowledge of logic, such as identifying common logical fallacies, helps in discerning the loopholes in false information and propaganda slogans.

2. Expanding Information Sources: Breaking the Information Cocoon

  • Using VPNs/Circumvention Tools (If Possible): Although there are risks, using tools like VPNs allows access to censored foreign information, providing a more comprehensive view and breaking the information blockade. Be sure to prioritize security, choose reputable VPN services, and protect personal privacy.
  • Following Independent Media and Commentators: Look for independent media and commentators who often provide perspectives and views different from official propaganda. However, also be mindful of verifying the truthfulness of the information and maintaining critical thinking.
  • Interacting with People from Different Backgrounds: Communicating with people from different backgrounds and with different views helps expand your horizons, understand diverse perspectives, and avoid falling into a single mode of thinking.

3. Protecting Personal Privacy: Speaking Cautiously, Paying Attention to Cybersecurity

  • Avoiding Sensitive Remarks in Public: In a high-pressure environment, one must speak carefully and cautiously, avoiding making any remarks that might cause trouble in public, including on social media.
  • Using Secure Communication Tools: Use encrypted communication software for private exchanges to prevent personal information from being monitored.
  • Paying Attention to Cybersecurity: Regularly change passwords, avoid clicking on unknown links, and prevent personal information leakage.

4. Learning History: Learning from the Past to Avoid Repeating Mistakes

  • Understanding the History of Totalitarianism: By reading history books and watching documentaries, one can understand the operation and dangers of totalitarianism, thereby increasing vigilance and avoiding past mistakes.
  • Focusing on Human Rights and Freedom: Paying attention to the international community’s focus on human rights and freedom, and understanding related laws and systems, helps in better protecting one’s own rights.

5. Maintaining Physical and Mental Health: Preserving Mental Independence

  • Maintaining an Optimistic Mindset: In a high-pressure environment, maintaining an optimistic mindset is crucial. Stress can be relieved through exercise, meditation, and other methods, helping to maintain physical and mental health.
  • Seeking Support: If feeling excessive stress, one can seek help and support from friends, family, or professionals.

6. Accumulating Strength, Waiting for the Opportunity: Never Giving Up Hope

  • Do Not Despair: Even in the darkest times, maintain hope, believing that change will eventually come.
  • Accumulating Strength: Within one’s personal capacity, do things that can be done, such as spreading the truth or supporting vulnerable groups.
  • Monitoring Social Changes: Closely observe social changes, waiting for the appropriate moment.

Important Tips:

  • Safety is always the priority. Before taking any action, be sure to carefully assess the risks and take necessary safety measures.
  • Do not try to fight the powerful totalitarian machine alone. Protecting yourself, accumulating strength, and waiting for the right time is the wiser choice.
  • These suggestions are designed to help individuals maintain independent thinking, protect themselves, and accumulate strength for future change in a high-pressure environment. Remember, even in the darkest moments, maintain hope, believing that light will eventually come.

The Simplest Way: Escape

item.title: The sole source of wealth: The value of production and time
item.description: Explore the true source of wealth and the importance of time as the ultimate means of production, revealing how to achieve financial freedom through production, sales, and investment.
item.content:encoded:
The Only Normal Source of Wealth is Production

However, the core reason why the vast majority of people fail is not because they don’t engage in production, nor is it because they never accumulate. Rather, it is because they fail to accumulate for a sufficiently long time, resulting in insufficient capital, and thus they fail to acquire or master true wealth.

Life should be centered around production. Everything else, no matter what it is, must be ranked after it. Nothing is more important than production—at least, until basic necessities are met.

What Exactly Are the Means of Production?

  • Time is the only means of production owned by the proletariat. Time is incompressible, time is uncrossable, and time is always indispensable.
  • You must produce goods and services that can be sold. In other words, someone needs them, or even the entire society needs them, for someone to buy them. Otherwise, how good you feel your creation is is useless. If no one wants it, there is no exchange, and therefore, there is no money.

The Fundamental Reason for Life’s Hardship

To make money, you must produce, because the only legitimate source of wealth is production; conversely, if you don’t produce, you won’t earn money. Fundamentally, the difference in people’s income primarily stems from the distance from effective production. In other words, the closer you are to production, the more money you earn; or conversely, the farther you are from production, the less money you earn.

The Jobs People Dislike Doing

In the past, apprentices mostly focused on the production process; but for today’s workers, the most profitable approach might be to choose the sales process—that is, working in a sales department.

The key here is that sales income has no upper limit. This is unmatched by any other organized form of effective production. The more developed the society, the larger the market, and the richer the variety of goods and services, the more essential sales become to the creators. Therefore, many sales positions have a “performance commission incentive mechanism”—how much you earn depends on your performance. Other positions, such as administration, accounting, and logistics, generally have fixed salaries. So, if you want to earn more, you should prioritize choosing sales.

Absurdly Selling the Means of Production

Time is our ultimate means of production. The tragic thing is that 99% of people rely on directly selling their time to earn income. For the vast majority of people, their personal business model throughout their lives is simply selling their time without any processing. Then, they desperately compete at this level, striving to have the highest unit price for their time—that’s all.

The Business Sense Not Taught in School

Customer Lifetime Value refers to the profit you can earn from a single customer who buys your product or service throughout their entire life.

  • The shorter the time cost, the harder it is to make money.

For a restaurant, it is actually a quite good business for the average person, and the probability of success is quite high. However, from the perspective of time cost, this business is not the most profitable. It has a certain learning time cost, and while the daily production time cost is not high, it requires continuous production, and every sale incurs a certain time cost.

In comparison,

Creating a book is relatively much more profitable because, although the learning time cost is relatively high (research and preparation), there is also some production time cost (the writing process). But the sales time cost and the reproduction time cost are zero for the author.

Money is a Social Ledger

  • From the essential nature of a social ledger, it can be seen that money is actually the debt of the entire society. It represents what society owes you or the services it owes you. If you are very poor and lack money, it actually represents that you owe society a lot. You have made little contribution to society.

  • Money can factually store anything, so, of course, money can also be a form of means of production storage.

  • Money is a means of production. And, it is simultaneously a form of storage.

  • Money is the most flexible means of production.

Money Has Two Different Uses

  • For most people, money has only one use: consumption.
  • The second, and far more important, use of money is: investment.

The desire to invest grows from nothing and becomes increasingly strong. It automatically overwhelms the desire to consume, to the point where, without realizing it, you naturally use more money for investment rather than consumption, unless it is a necessary consumption.

Consumption is naturally joyful because desires are satisfied. But actually, investment is also joyful; it is also a way of satisfying desires, and perhaps it should be even more joyful.

Knowledge is like this, and useful knowledge is even more so. Once you learn it, you cannot forget it. It is difficult for you now to waste money carelessly because you feel it should be used to produce; it is difficult for you to hate the rich because you know they are creditors; it is difficult for you to ignore financial management because you know money is the storage of all things, and your freedom is stored there; it is difficult for you to be content with simply selling your time because you know that is the worst personal business model;

The Fundamental Principle of Producing with Money

The essence of investment is actually lending and receiving interest. Even the core of finance is merely interest; and the entire financial market is driven by and exists solely because of interest rates.

  • Money is actually a form of means of production.
  • Interest is the compensation for the opportunity cost of capital.

Just like time, capital is an exclusive resource. This means that its use incurs an opportunity cost.

Regarding Borrowing Money

All money lent to relatives and friends is essentially given away; do not expect them to pay it back.

People who know how to produce with money cannot just lend money out casually because their opportunity cost is relatively higher. Upon deeper reflection, many people lend money to others not because they consider themselves generous or benevolent, but because of ignorance or incompetence. The opportunity cost of the money they hold is actually zero, so they don’t care much. Of course, this statement is difficult to hear, but the logic is sound.

Equity is Essentially Equivalent to Debt

  • From the company’s perspective, the company has borrowed a sum of money that never needs to be repaid.
  • From the lender’s perspective, there are suddenly many benefits: higher returns and stronger liquidity.

The Fundamental Difference Between Investment and Speculation

In the stock market, all investors are traders, but factually, not all traders are investors. Only a tiny minority of traders follow a long-term holding strategy, while the vast majority of traders engage in frequent trading. What is the difference? Only investors consider time as a necessary component of the means of production, whereas the vast majority of traders—let’s call them “speculators”—do not have time in their means of production.

Time is the Only Path to Development.

Traders play completely different games in the same arena. Speculators participate in what I believe is the worst kind of limited game, called a “zero-sum game”: the money earned is actually the money lost by others. But investors are different; if they succeed, they earn the “result of development.” What they participate in is actually an “infinite game.”

The Mirror Effect of Investment Risk

I am too lazy to even look at financial reports because the best companies are the ones that fake their financial reports the least. I have a background in accounting, so it’s not that I can’t understand financial reports; I just feel that picking stocks by looking at financial reports is like trying to find gold in a pile of garbage. But the problem is, the gold mountain is standing right there, so why bother? The way ordinary people choose stocks is simple: first, try to choose the best goods in life. Then, not only buy the goods, but also buy the stock simultaneously.

The Actual Shape of Individual Time

Time is like a container, and inside it are all the people who have lived up to the present, and all the things they have done. Obviously, the size of each person’s time container is different.

This container of time has a starting point and an endpoint, but between the start and the end, time is more like a pipeline than just a straight line. Some people do more things in a unit of time and are more efficient; therefore, this person’s time is different from others’ time—it has a larger diameter, a thicker pipe. Some people do nothing meaningful for a long time; in that period, this person’s time is merely a straight line.

What should we do to make money? Produce, sell, invest. In any case, we absolutely cannot waste this ultimate means of production, time, on things that yield no output.

How to Do More Things

  • After spending time to earn money, we must do more things.
  • More precious than financial freedom is actually time freedom.

For those without production capacity, time is merely a ray—instantaneously having no area, long-term having no volume; time is not really a means of production. Therefore, time can only be “bored,” bored to the point of “waste,” and must reach the point of being “killed.” For those with production capacity, time is simply too beautiful; it can be used to create anything, do countless things, and even family affection or love can be “fermented” with time. Furthermore, as production efficiency increases, the possibilities of time become more numerous and greater. This is probably the most exciting reason why we are obsessed with learning and unwilling to learn any skill!

Factors Acting Against Production

If you are a producer, or even an effective producer, or even just someone aspiring to be a producer, you must know that there are things that are naturally “anti-production” and absolutely must be avoided. First are drugs and gambling. The ultimate victims of these two things are likely to start innocently, based on the naive idea of “just trying” or “just playing,” holding the侥幸 (lucky chance) mentality that “it won’t happen again.” Little do they know, these two things should not even be touched.

Of course, more common than drugs and gambling is vanity. The definition of vanity can be very clear: money used for consumption was not earned through one’s own production, yet one is not ashamed of it but is proud of it.

Wealth Index = Own Production Income / Own Consumption Expenditure

  • If a person’s Wealth Index = 1, they are neither poor nor rich;
  • If Wealth Index < 1, they are poor, and the smaller the Wealth Index, the poorer they are;
  • If Wealth Index > 1, they are wealthy, and the larger the Wealth Index, the richer they are.

Many so-called wealthy people have the actual dilemma that their consumption expenditure is very high, while their production income is equal to 0, or even less than 0.

Some people genuinely earn money through effective production, but they often fall back into poverty—as the old saying goes, “Seeing the high building, seeing the banquet, seeing the building collapse.” The core reason for falling back into poverty is always the same: the growth rate of consumption expenditure far exceeds the growth rate of production income.

In my words, never increase your consumption level too quickly.

In the more than 40 years since the Reform and Opening Up, a large number of so-called “middle classes” have appeared. But once the economy declines, the vast majority of them fall back into poverty overnight. What happened? It’s not that they didn’t earn money; their problem is that they earned money but failed to control their spending. Too many expenditures in life are not necessities but stem from desires from various angles. Desire has no end; if it is not properly controlled, it actually has the power to make anyone fall back into poverty, no matter how strong their production capacity is.

Wealth Gap is Inevitable

Every sedan requires at least 4 people to carry it; there must inevitably be poor people, and society needs poor people to function normally.

Basic Principles for Improving Efficiency

The act of learning actually includes at least four levels: learning, practicing, applying, and creating. Therefore, just learning without practicing is a waste of time and is the fundamental reason why most people fail to learn. What you learn, you must use; what you learn, you must practice. The process of practice is actually the only way to improve efficiency. Through massive iteration (not just repetition), continuous accumulation, and continuous improvement. Efficiency can never happen overnight, because efficiency must be developed.

Unexpected things will certainly happen in life, and you will encounter bad people and bad events, but these are external factors. Their existence or appearance has already damaged my development; you absolutely cannot let them further devour my ultimate means of production. After all, all my wealth, whether material or spiritual, comes from my time, or more accurately, from the volume of my time. What time do I have to waste? What reason do I have to waste it on them? At all times, focusing on improving efficiency is the main thing.

Summary

  • Wealth comes from production, and it comes from oneself;
  • Time is the ultimate means of production;
  • Money is the storage of all things;
  • Money is the most flexible means of production.

In this increasingly better era, as long as you spend your time on self-study, production, sales, and investment, you can earn money, and there are still many things worth doing.

item.title: Why I Chose the S&P 500 as My Primary Investment Asset
item.description:
Throughout my investment journey, I have come to trust the S&P 500 and consider it the core of my wealth storage. By understanding the US Constitution, the free society, and the powerful military behind it, I believe that the S&P 500 represents the strongest companies and the most stable economy in the world. Here’s why I made this decision and the thinking behind it:

The US Constitution and Free Society are the Strongest Guarantees

I firmly believe that the US Constitution and the free society structure are among the most valuable assets in the world. The rule of law and the powerful military, particularly the aircraft carrier, provide a unique guarantee for global investors. If the US Constitution protects investors’ rights and the economy relies on the free market, it will provide a solid foundation for my chosen assets.
item.content:encoded:
Throughout my investment journey, I have come to trust the S&P 500 and consider it the core of my wealth storage. By understanding the US Constitution, the free society, and the powerful military behind it, I believe that the S&P 500 represents the strongest companies and the most stable economy in the world. Here’s why I made this decision and the thinking behind it:

The US Constitution and Free Society are the Strongest Guarantees

I firmly believe that the US Constitution and the free society structure are among the most valuable assets in the world. The rule of law and the powerful military, particularly the aircraft carrier, provide a unique guarantee for global investors. If the US Constitution protects investors’ rights and the economy relies on the free market, it will provide a solid foundation for my chosen assets.

Globally, while other countries have excellent companies, they are not protected by a constitution and military power like the US. The US Constitution makes it a special economy, and this guarantee allows American companies to occupy an important position globally. Therefore, I think choosing the S&P 500 is not just choosing a basket of top global companies, but also choosing a system protected by the US Constitution and military power.

S&P 500 Represents the Strongest Global Companies

The S&P 500 is not a single “stock” asset; it is a collective symbol of the 500 strongest companies in the world. These companies are leaders in multiple industries and have global competitiveness. Their strength is not only reflected in their market share and financial performance but also in the stable, law-based, free market, and powerful military behind them.

I believe that the 500 companies represented by the S&P 500 not only occupy a leading position in finance and technology globally but also enjoy the protection of the US Constitution and powerful military. This is why I think the S&P 500 has a unique advantage that no other asset can match.

Market Fluctuations and Long-term Beliefs

Although the S&P 500 has experienced several market crashes, such as the 2008 financial crisis and the 2020 COVID-19 pandemic, I believe these are just short-term fluctuations. In the long term, the fundamentals of the S&P 500 have not changed; it still represents the strong economic power and corporate competitiveness of the US. Therefore, during market crashes, my decision is not to sell the S&P 500 but to hold it firmly. Even if the market experiences temporary crashes, I do not think any other asset can replace the S&P 500 as a long-term value storage tool.

Many investors choose to sell assets and exchange them for cash during market crashes, but I think the value of cash is far less than the S&P 500. In my view, the S&P 500 is the most valuable asset globally, while cash depreciates over time due to inflation. Therefore, unless it’s for necessary living expenses, I choose to focus my wealth on the S&P 500 and not sell it easily.

Diversification and Risk Management

Although I have unwavering trust in the S&P 500, I still maintain a certain level of diversification. In my asset allocation, I invest 90% of my wealth in the S&P 500 and the remaining 10% in the PIMCO Enhanced Short Maturity Active ETF (MINT), which has high liquidity. This configuration not only maintains the growth potential of most of my assets but also provides additional liquidity and risk cushion during market fluctuations.

I chose MINT because it represents low risk and stable returns. This part of my assets can help me maintain a certain level of cash flow during market turbulence, allowing me to respond to unforeseen emergencies or adjustments.

Why Not Diversify into Other Markets or Assets?

Many investment experts recommend diversifying investments to reduce risk, such as investing in international markets, gold, or real estate. However, I firmly believe that no country or market can be stronger than the US. The US Constitution and free society are the foundation of my trust, and the US military power and aircraft carriers fleet provide a unique safety guarantee for global investors. In this context, I think the S&P 500 not only represents the top 500 companies in the world but also the strongest economy and military system globally.

Although I understand the importance of diversification, due to my firm trust in the US free society and Constitution, I believe the S&P 500 is the most valuable and worthy long-term holding asset globally. Therefore, I do not tend to diversify my assets into other markets or assets like gold, as they do not have the same guarantees and potential as the S&P 500.

How to Face Uncertainty and Challenges?

Although I have deep trust in the S&P 500, I am not complacent about the changes in the global economic situation and political landscape. Although I do not have in-depth knowledge of global geopolitics and international trade conflicts, I remain rational and calm. I cannot predict every market fluctuation, I can rely on long-term investment strategies to cope with these uncertainties.

For me, the core of long-term investment is patience, trust, and determination. Even if the global economy undergoes drastic changes, I will rely on my trust in the S&P 500 and the US system, continue to hold it, and not make emotional decisions due to short-term fluctuations.

Conclusion: Rational Investment, Firm Beliefs

Through this period of thinking and investment decision-making, I have established my own investment philosophy: the S&P 500 is not just a stock market index, but a representation of my trust in the US Constitution, free society, and powerful military. I choose to invest most of my wealth in the S&P 500 and maintain a long-term holding strategy because it represents the top companies and the most stable economy globally.

Although I know that global economic and political risks are unavoidable, I believe the S&P 500 is the most worthy long-term holding asset. If the market crashes in the future, I will firmly believe in my decision and not sell easily, but instead, choose to wait patiently for the market to recover.

Epilogue

Through in-depth analysis of the logic behind the S&P 500, I am confident in my investment decisions. Long-term market fluctuations cannot shake my trust in the US Constitution and free society, which has given me a more firm belief in my investment path. In my future investment journey, I will continue to adhere to this philosophy, maintain sensitivity to market changes, and continuously increase my knowledge to better cope with potential risks.

item.title: The essence of the highest and lowest points
item.description:
The Market is Only Equivalent to a Person of Average Intelligence

As a participant in the trading market, you are unlikely to sell at the peak, and it is also difficult to buy at the trough…

Why? The reason is very clear and simple:

Humans are Impulsive and Emotional

The peak and the trough are both caused by the “impulse” of a small portion of traders…

You are destined to be a non-impulsive person, so that impulsive trading is destined not to belong to the non-impulsive you! Believe me, you are a normal person, so it is very normal for you to occasionally experience a little hallucination. However, you are different. Where is the difference? item.title: The essence of reducing trading frequency
item.description: This paper discusses the relationship between trading frequency and the investment risk-return ratio. It emphasizes that reducing trading frequency can avoid the accumulation of transaction fees and minimize unnecessary risk, thereby improving the rationality and returns of long-term investment.
item.content:encoded:
Frequency is the Fundamental Factor That Determines Everything

In the short term, it is the voting machine; in the long term, it is the weighing machine.

The Higher the Trading Frequency, the Closer the Trade is to a Zero-Sum Game

The result of frequent trading is the accumulation of transaction fees, which eventually consumes all your profits and principal.

The shorter the prediction, the closer it is to flipping a coin;

The longer the prediction, the closer it is to true logical deduction…

Therefore, the essence of reducing trading frequency is refusing to flip a coin and insisting on logical deduction.

Risk-Reward Ratio

The Risk-Reward Ratio (or Risk-Return Ratio) is an important concept in investment and trading, used to measure the expected return for every unit of risk assumed. It reflects the relationship between the risk and the potential reward of a trading opportunity or investment decision.

Risk-Reward Ratio = Potential Return ÷ Assumed Risk

Potential Return: Refers to the target profit, which is the amount you hope to gain in the trade. For example, if you buy a stock, you expect it to rise to a certain price; the potential return is the difference between that price and the purchase price.

Assumed Risk: Refers to the maximum possible loss you are willing to take, usually determined by the stop-loss price. For example, after buying a stock, you set a stop-loss price; the assumed risk is the difference between the stop-loss price and the purchase price.

  • Challenges of High Trading Frequency: Frequent trading makes the “Risk-Reward Ratio” of every trade lower. This is because the probability of achieving a massive return in a short period is very low. Even if the market occasionally experiences violent fluctuations (sudden surge or crash), attempting to capture this volatility carries extremely high risk—it is like “picking chestnuts out of the fire”—and easily leads to losses.

  • The Concept of Risk-Reward Ratio: The Risk-Reward Ratio refers to the potential return that can be brought by a unit of risk. If trading frequently, the potential return of each trade is often not large enough, yet the risk always exists, making it difficult to improve the Risk-Reward Ratio.

The Significance of Actively Reducing Trading Frequency

Active vs. Passive:

  • Active reduction of trading frequency is an action where the trader controls the pace, indicating that the trader is controlling the market rhythm, rather than being dragged along by short-term market fluctuations.
  • Conversely, “unconsciously frequent trading” is a passive reaction driven by market sentiment, usually manifesting as the trader fearing missing out (FOMO) or rushing to chase short-term volatility.

How to Improve the Risk-Reward Ratio: Actively reducing trading frequency actually indirectly improves the Risk-Reward Ratio:

  • Denominator (Risk) remains unchanged: The risk you assume has not increased.
  • Numerator (Return) increases: By reducing frequency, you focus on opportunities with greater potential, increasing the expectation of potential return.

item.title: Leek Destiny
item.description:
Exhaustion of Entry Capital

There are many frustrating laws in the trading market, such as:

  • Whenever you need money, the market crashes!
  • It might not seem logically supported, so you might temporarily doubt it, but you will definitely experience the magic of this law.
  • For all beginners, this law is almost eternally true:
  • As soon as you buy, it starts to fall;
  • As soon as you sell, it starts to rise…

Why does this paradoxical situation occur? Because the fundamental reason for the end of every market trend is the exhaustion of entry capital. In other words, when even the auntie selling tea eggs on the street starts discussing stocks, the market’s “entry capital” is already on the verge of depletion… Think about it, even you, who are completely unrelated to this, know that when it’s time to rush in and make money, the market trend is over, right?
item.content:encoded:
Exhaustion of Entry Capital

There are many frustrating laws in the trading market, such as:

  • Whenever you need money, the market crashes!
  • It might not seem logically supported, so you might temporarily doubt it, but you will definitely experience the magic of this law.
  • For all beginners, this law is almost eternally true:
  • As soon as you buy, it starts to fall;
  • As soon as you sell, it starts to rise…

Why does this paradoxical situation occur? Because the fundamental reason for the end of every market trend is the exhaustion of entry capital. In other words, when even the auntie selling tea eggs on the street starts discussing stocks, the market’s “entry capital” is already on the verge of depletion… Think about it, even you, who are completely unrelated to this, know that when it’s time to rush in and make money, the market trend is over, right?

Remedying the Loss Requires a Prerequisite

  • You don’t just have the one sheep that was lost;
  • Besides it, you should have many other sheep;
  • Because you have many sheep, you must have built a “sheep pen” in the past;
  • Therefore, even though you have “lost a sheep,” you still have a chance to “repair the pen”;
  • Therefore, once the “pen” is repaired, you can manage more sheep;
  • Therefore, the loss of one or two sheep initially is negligible to the final result.
  • Therefore, what should the “leek” (retail investor) who “lost the sheep” do? It’s simple:
  • If you have money, slowly add to your position (top up);
  • If you don’t have enough money, desperately make money outside the market.

Controlling Position Size

You must always reserve a certain proportion or at least a certain quantity of cash—this is non-negotiable, just like a diver needs an oxygen tank. As for what that proportion or quantity should be, there is no fixed theorem; it is entirely up to you to figure it out.

This viewpoint primarily emphasizes the necessity of controlling position size and holding cash. Here is the reasoning and logical analysis:

1. Flexibility of Cash: Dealing with Unknown Risks

In the investment market, risk is unavoidable, and market fluctuations can happen at any time. If you invest all your funds in the market without keeping cash reserves, you might find yourself in a passive position when the market experiences a sharp decline or an emergency situation:

  • Preventing Forced Selling: If the market suddenly drops, holding cash allows you to avoid being forced to sell assets at a low point.
  • Handling Emergencies: Cash is the most liquid asset, which can be used at any time to deal with sudden needs, whether it’s an urgent living expense or an investment opportunity.

2. Cash is the “Oxygen Tank”: Avoiding Full Position Risk

  • Comparing cash to an “oxygen tank” highlights its lifeline significance, especially during extreme market volatility:
  • Buffering Effect: The market environment might be full of pressure, like deep underwater; cash reserves provide you with breathing room during a crisis.
  • Psychological Comfort: Holding a certain amount of cash gives you a greater sense of security during market fluctuations, reducing the possibility of making wrong decisions due to panic.

3. Seizing Opportunities: “Ammunition” During Market Downturns

The market is cyclical, and opportunities for undervaluation always arise. If all your funds are invested in the market without keeping cash, you might not be able to utilize the opportunity when it appears:

  • Averaging Down (Buying on Dip): During market downturns, those with cash can buy quality assets at lower prices.
  • Asset Appreciation Potential: This “ammunition” can help you achieve higher returns when the market recovers.

Excellent, Successful Traders Are Ultimately Risk Averse

  • Watch other people taking risks! Sometimes the “correct conclusion” looks so sinister, even shining brightly in the deepest parts.

Extreme Fear of Missing Opportunities

Fear of Missing Out, abbreviated as FOMO, is also known as Fear of Missing Opportunity.

FOMO, “Extreme Fear of Missing Opportunity.” FOMO is almost the most widespread phenomenon, and the more fundamental it is, the easier it is to be swayed by it. Just look at the slogans used by pyramid schemes or micro-businesses, and you’ll see they are almost always the same:

You missed XXX, and then you missed YYY, and now you want to miss ZZZ?!

The people who lack opportunities the most are the easiest to be incited by such phrases. Calm down and think about it, and you will understand: if you are a person who is not lacking opportunities, even if the price of Bitcoin skyrockets, will you feel anxious because of that fact? No! Because you have other opportunities.

Solitude is the Most Precious Quality of a Successful Trader

If you are not good at entertaining yourself, if you do not spend a large amount of time living a serious life, then you cannot reduce your trading frequency, and you will become like a leek staring at the screen all day, keeping your phone within reach even when having sex with your girlfriend—then failure is inevitable.

Experts do not prioritize “correctness,” because anyone can be correct; this is not a particularly difficult thing. The truly difficult thing is that you are not only correct, but you are uniquely correct. Only by being “unconventional and correct” can you generate huge trading value.

Consensus May Create Price (Though Not Necessarily Value)

item.title: No risk, no reward.
item.description:
Risk is a Necessity

Many risks are unavoidable. What we should do is assess the risks and then take them. Some risks are not worth taking, no matter how high the potential return is.

Risk Assessment

I. What is your ultimate goal? If achieved, what kind of situation will it be? II. How can you achieve your goal with no risk or minimal risk? In other words, what elements can guarantee you reach your target smoothly? III. Are the above no-risk options feasible or desirable? If not, how much risk do you need to take to get what you want?
item.content:encoded:
Risk is a Necessity

Many risks are unavoidable. What we should do is assess the risks and then take them. Some risks are not worth taking, no matter how high the potential return is.

Risk Assessment

I. What is your ultimate goal? If achieved, what kind of situation will it be? II. How can you achieve your goal with no risk or minimal risk? In other words, what elements can guarantee you reach your target smoothly? III. Are the above no-risk options feasible or desirable? If not, how much risk do you need to take to get what you want?

Hedging (Risk Aversion)

A set of strategies that minimizes risk is hedging (or risk aversion). Hedging protects you from losses through balancing measures, seeking equilibrium between risk and safety, much like a woman in a brothel. Alternatively, hedging might be like placing two bets simultaneously, where in a win-only scenario, you ultimately forgo some potential profit to offset potential losses. Another way to reduce risk is through insurance, paying others to bear the downside risk (Note 11). The difference from hedging is that after paying the premium, you retain the full expected benefit. Risk management reduces the probability of the worst-case scenario, but it also brings a disadvantage. Any tool that reduces risk can also be used to increase risk: a safety net can catch you when you fall, but it can also become a trampoline that launches you high up; hedging and insurance are the same. Not only that, reducing risk can allow you to take risks with confidence, ultimately aiming for big gains by taking small risks.

Control Your Emotions, Become the Master of Risk

Utilize risk management strategies to reduce your reaction to losses and maintain a consistent attitude when taking risks. This way, you will absolutely not suffer too many losses, and you can remain fully focused on achieving success.

item.title: Even if you don't like reality, you must acknowledge reality.
item.description:
People Dislike Hearing Bad News

Or anything that contradicts their existing views and conclusions. Therefore, if certain things might be painful, the human brain will start to act and try to deny reality. Psychologist Daniel Kahneman, a Nobel laureate, believes: “People don’t even want to put in the minimal effort to figure out what they did wrong; this is not accidental, but because they simply don’t want to know.”

Everyone Avoids It

We all invent stories for ourselves and evade the facts. Even if you spend a lot of time studying behavioral economics, your skills might only improve slightly. You will always make mistakes. People often ignore or refuse to admit the faults of those they love, and tend to distort the facts to accommodate their loved ones.

Some people are clearly criminals, obvious without needing analysis or inference, yet their mother insists that her son is innocent. This is simple psychological denial. Reality is too painful to bear, so you must distort it in order to endure it. To some extent, we all do this; it is a common psychological misjudgment, but it causes serious problems.

item.title: Reading "The Old Man and the Sea": Why I Gave It One Star?
item.description: Although this book is highly acclaimed in literary circles, from a personal perspective, I do not feel a strong emotional resonance with The Old Man and the Sea. My initial feeling is that the story of this book does not move me. The actions of the old man, Santiago, in my view are reckless and irrational. His persistence and spirit of not giving up, on the contrary, make me feel a sense of aversion. I believe that his battle with the large fish was irrational, as he ignored potential risks and failures, and failed to stop the adventure in time. From the perspective of economics and rational decision-making, this behavior is flawed. His sunk cost is too high, and since there is nothing left to gain, he still insists on going all the way.
item.content:encoded:
Although this book is highly acclaimed in literary circles, from a personal perspective, I do not feel a strong emotional resonance with The Old Man and the Sea. My initial feeling is that the story of this book does not move me. The actions of the old man, Santiago, in my view are reckless and irrational. His persistence and spirit of not giving up, on the contrary, make me feel a sense of aversion. I believe that his battle with the large fish was irrational, as he ignored potential risks and failures, and failed to stop the adventure in time. From the perspective of economics and rational decision-making, this behavior is flawed. His sunk cost is too high, and since there is nothing left to gain, he still insists on going all the way.

Personal Thought Process

Initial Feeling: Lack of Resonance

When I first started reading The Old Man and the Sea, I did not feel a strong emotional resonance. Santiago’s resilience and tenacity seem to be quite different from my personal life philosophy. Although he did not give up for three days and nights and finally caught the giant fish, I felt doubtful about his stubborn behavior. In my opinion, Santiago’s adventure is full of irrationality; he disregards potential risks and the possibility of failure, ultimately leading to unnecessary losses.

Reflection from an Economic Perspective

As someone who emphasizes rational decision-making, my first reaction is that this old man’s behavior has major flaws. In investment and wealth management, cutting losses, identifying risks, and timely strategy adjustment are key to success. Santiago’s behavior undoubtedly contradicts this philosophy; he is too persistent with his “sunk cost” and does not give up at the appropriate moment. Ultimately, even though he won the struggle, the cost he paid due to the attack by sharks was greater than the benefit. This behavior reminds me of some “fighting until the end” practices in life, especially when one is unwilling to correct a wrong decision, which can lead to even greater losses.

Conflict Between Rational Decision-Making and the “Never Give Up” Spirit

The “never give up” spirit in The Old Man and the Sea forms a stark contrast with the rational decision-making philosophy that I advocate. In modern society, especially in the investment field, rationality and flexible response are more emphasized than sheer persistence and struggle. I believe that facing challenges, timely admitting mistakes, cutting losses, and adjusting strategies is a more rational and efficient approach. Santiago’s behavior in the book seems somewhat impractical and outdated.

Relationship Between Classic Literature and the Historical Context

The Old Man and the Sea was born during the Cold War era of the 1950s. Literature of that era often focused on individual will and the struggle for survival. At that time, many people admired the spirit of unyielding struggle, whereas modern society places more emphasis on rational thinking and effective decision-making. Santiago’s persistence reflects the emphasis on individual spirit and the meaning of struggle during the Cold War, but this may no longer be so suitable for our modern lifestyle and values.

Critical Understanding: The Collision of Classicism and Personal Values

Difference Between Personal Understanding and the Classic

My low evaluation of The Old Man and the Sea does not mean that I cannot understand its value; rather, it reflects the conflict between my values and the spirit of the book. I do not endorse Santiago’s decision-making style, believing that his stubborn adventure that ultimately resulted in loss is not worthy of praise. As a proponent of rational decision-making, I believe that timely loss cutting and strategy adjustment are the wisest choices. My view does not mean that I lack literary literacy; rather, it is an independent interpretation of the classic work from the perspective of modern society.

Reflection on the Classic Work and Its Value

Classic literary works are not perfect; they often challenge our ways of thinking and living. Through critical reading, we can not only understand the work itself but also recognize our own life philosophy and decision-making principles on a deeper level. For me, The Old Man and the Sea is not a simple judgment of “good” or “bad,” but a work that inspires thought and makes me reflect on rational decision-making and life attitude.

Conclusion: Independent Thought and Personal Reading Journey

Overall, although I do not feel an emotional resonance with The Old Man and the Sea nor do I endorse its “never give up” spirit, I still believe it is a work worth contemplating. Through the critical reading of this book, I have further solidified my values of rational decision-making and timely loss cutting. The significance of classic literature lies not in whether it conforms to every reader’s philosophy, but in its ability to inspire us to deeply reflect on life, decisions, and principles.

I do not believe that I have “misunderstood” Hemingway, or that my evaluation of the work is flawed. On the contrary, it is precisely this independent thought about classic works that makes my reading journey richer and allows me to gain a deeper understanding of my own life philosophy and decision-making methods.
