First, we can look at how people get into trouble because of what they say.

Only if two conditions are met simultaneously.

The first condition is that the words cannot be said;

The second condition is that they are correct, or seem likely to be correct and are worth further discussion. If the second condition is not met, in most cases, you won’t have trouble.

If you say that 2+2 equals 5, or that the average height of a citizen in Pittsburgh is three meters, you won’t have any issues. These obviously incorrect statements might be taken as a joke, or worse, as proof that you are crazy, but they certainly won’t anger anyone.

Statements that anger others are those that people might believe.

I hypothesize that the most infuriating statements are those believed to be telling the truth. If Galileo said that the people of Padua are three meters tall, he would only be regarded as a quirky, mad scientist.

But, when he said that the Earth revolves around the Sun, the nature of it was completely different.

The Church knew that this kind of statement would make people start thinking.

item.title: Zhu Yuanzhang used the Yellow Registers (Huangce) and Travel Permits (Luyin) to confine farmers to the land. Why did these policies become ineffective later?
item.description:
In the mid-to-late Ming Dynasty, due to the development of the socio-economy and population growth, farmers’ demand for land increased. However, the uneven distribution of land and the heavy burden of taxes made it impossible for many farmers to maintain a livelihood. Therefore, they began seeking ways to improve their lives, such as temporary registration (jiji), wandering/migrating (youyu), or engaging in maritime commerce (xiahai jingshang) 12.

In the mid-to-late Ming Dynasty, due to the corruption of officials and lax supervision, the management of the Yellow Registers and travel permits became chaotic and riddled with loopholes. Phenomena such as fraudulent registration (maoji), fake household registration (jiaji), and privately manufactured travel permits were frequently observed, causing the household registration system to lose its regulatory power 12.
item.content:encoded:
In the mid-to-late Ming Dynasty, due to the development of the socio-economy and population growth, farmers’ demand for land increased. However, the uneven distribution of land and the heavy burden of taxes made it impossible for many farmers to maintain a livelihood. Therefore, they began seeking ways to improve their lives, such as temporary registration (jiji), wandering/migrating (youyu), or engaging in maritime commerce (xiahai jingshang) 12.

In the mid-to-late Ming Dynasty, due to the corruption of officials and lax supervision, the management of the Yellow Registers and travel permits became chaotic and riddled with loopholes. Phenomena such as fraudulent registration (maoji), fake household registration (jiaji), and privately manufactured travel permits were frequently observed, causing the household registration system to lose its regulatory power 12.

In the mid-to-late Ming Dynasty, due to causes such as natural disasters, warfare, and epidemics, many regions experienced sharp population decline, missing household registrations, and land abandonment. This caused the data in the Yellow Registers and travel permits to severely mismatch the actual situation, making it impossible to reflect the true population dynamics 1.

item.title: What are the defining changes as a dynasty moves from its middle phase to its final years?
item.description:
As a dynasty moves from its middle period towards its late years, it is often accompanied by a series of characteristic changes. Here are some common changes:

Political Instability and Power Struggles: As time passes, the dynasty’s governance often experiences instability and power struggles. Political corruption, unfair official appointments, and the phenomenon of vying for power may intensify, leading to internal political instability and chaos.

Territorial Retreat and War Challenges: In its late years, the dynasty may face territorial shrinkage, losing control over certain regions. External forces may launch wars, challenging the dynasty’s territory. This can lead to the weakening of the nation’s military strength and a reduction in territory.
item.content:encoded:
As a dynasty moves from its middle period towards its late years, it is often accompanied by a series of characteristic changes. Here are some common changes:

Political Instability and Power Struggles: As time passes, the dynasty’s governance often experiences instability and power struggles. Political corruption, unfair official appointments, and the phenomenon of vying for power may intensify, leading to internal political instability and chaos.

Territorial Retreat and War Challenges: In its late years, the dynasty may face territorial shrinkage, losing control over certain regions. External forces may launch wars, challenging the dynasty’s territory. This can lead to the weakening of the nation’s military strength and a reduction in territory.

Economic Decline and Fiscal Difficulties: The late years of a dynasty are often accompanied by economic recession and financial hardship. Reduced tax revenue and insufficient fiscal income to support national operations lead to rising prices, heavier taxation, and social poverty. Economic difficulties may result in social instability and public dissatisfaction.

Social Unrest and Popular Uprisings: With the arrival of the late dynasty, social unrest and popular uprisings may occur frequently. Phenomena such as peasant rebellions, waves of migration, and local fragmentation (or regional warlordism) may intensify, posing a serious threat to the stability of the central government. These uprisings and unrest are often a strong resistance against government corruption, exploitation, and oppression.

Cultural Decline and Knowledge Atrophy: The late dynasty is often accompanied by cultural decline and intellectual atrophy. Fields such as academic research, literary arts, and technological innovation may be negatively affected, and the social cultural life and knowledge inheritance are suppressed.

These changes are common characteristics of a dynasty’s late years, but the specific situation varies depending on the history, region, and specific dynasty. The late years of a dynasty are often a stage of decline and demise, bearing obvious signs of recession and collapse.

item.title: Why are the late years of a dynasty often accompanied by economic decline and fiscal difficulties?
item.description:
There are multiple factors that can lead to the economic decline and fiscal difficulties at the end of a dynasty:

Negligence and Political Corruption of Rulers: At the end of a dynasty, issues of negligence and political corruption among rulers often intensify. Phenomena such as official corruption, bribery, and improper appointments lead to a decline in government efficiency, making it unable to effectively manage the national finances and economy. Such corrupt practices weaken fiscal revenue, resulting in financial difficulties.
item.content:encoded:
There are multiple factors that can lead to the economic decline and fiscal difficulties at the end of a dynasty:

Negligence and Political Corruption of Rulers: At the end of a dynasty, issues of negligence and political corruption among rulers often intensify. Phenomena such as official corruption, bribery, and improper appointments lead to a decline in government efficiency, making it unable to effectively manage the national finances and economy. Such corrupt practices weaken fiscal revenue, resulting in financial difficulties.

Excessive Taxation and Intensified Exploitation: To fill the fiscal deficit, the imperial court often increases the burden of taxes and the collection of other tribute goods. This places a heavy burden on farmers and merchants, leading to hindered economic development, decreased productivity, and even sparking social discontent and protests.

Obstruction of Domestic and International Trade and Market Contraction: The late dynasty often faces issues of obstructed domestic and international trade. Internal unrest and external wars lead to the interruption of transportation and trade routes, affecting the circulation of goods and the development of the market economy. Market contraction reduces commercial activities, further exacerbating the economic decline.

Decline in Agricultural Production and Frequent Disasters: Agriculture is the foundation of a dynastic economy, but at the end of a dynasty, agricultural production often declines. Factors such as long-term warfare, land abandonment, and peasant uprisings lead to a decrease in agricultural productivity. Simultaneously, natural disasters such as drought, floods, and locust plagues occur frequently, resulting in reduced or destroyed crops, further weakening the economic foundation.

Social Instability and Warfare Affecting Investment and Development: The late dynasty is often accompanied by social instability and warfare. Turbulent situations, such as internal rebellions, external threats, and peasant uprisings, hinder investment and development. Merchants and landlords may be reluctant to invest in economic development or transfer their assets, leading to a decline in economic vitality.

These factors interact to cause the economic decline and fiscal difficulties at the end of a dynasty. The combination of rulers’ negligence and political corruption, excessive taxation and exploitation, trade obstruction, agricultural decline, and social upheaval collectively leads to economic distress and fiscal collapse.

item.title: The Five Parts of Every Business
item.description:
1. Creates and delivers something of value . .
2. That other people want or need . . .
3. At a price they’re willing to pay . . .
4. In a way that satisfies the customer’s needs and expectations . . .
5. So that the business brings in enough profit to make it worthwhile for the owners to continue operation.

item.title: Creating one or two extraordinary and exceptional major cases at the right time is the most effective way to serve as a deterrent and instill fear.
item.description: The law of Duke Shang (Shang Jun) is that those who are punished and treated lightly (or discarded as ash on the path). The “discarded as ash” refers to minor offenses, while being punished refers to severe penalties. He (the law/system) is only clear in that it can deeply supervise minor offenses. If the offenses are minor and the supervision is deep, how much more so for severe offenses? Therefore, the people dare not commit them.

item.title: The Emperor is a terrorist
item.description: Fear makes bureaucracy more efficient, makes the common people more disciplined, makes the ruler’s benevolence easier for people to remember, and thus makes the ruler safer. Machiavelli says, “It is safer to be feared than to be loved.” A monarch who does not know how to “establish authority through killing” will eventually be looked down upon by the governed. Furthermore, benevolence and tolerance are only cherished and praised by the people when set against a backdrop of terror and severity. Therefore, a successful ruler must possess two sides: one side is the benevolence of a saint, the other is the cruelty of a lion.

item.title: Deep winter has arrived, a small suggestion.
item.description:
1. When you aren’t starving (or facing basic needs), nothing is an absolute necessity.
  2. Absolutely don’t think about catching the bottom (buying the dip); there might still be a garage below the -18th floor, and this money isn’t something you can earn.
  3. If you don’t invest in fixed assets, the holding costs for heavy assets are very high.
  4. Don’t start a business/venture; setting up a street stall is fine, but absolutely do not register a company.
  5. Don’t engage in virtual economies and virtual currencies.
  6. Save some emergency funds. They shouldn’t all be in RMB.

item.title: Ming Dynasty Core Values
item.description: As early as the Ming Dynasty, village heads and street entrances across various regions were erected with “Six Precepts Lying Steles” (or “Six Teachings Reclining Steles”). The content consists of the “Twenty-Four Characters of Moral Norms” stipulated by the Ming Taizu, Zhu Yuanzhang, for the common people: “Filial piety to parents, respect for elders, harmony in the village, educating children, ensuring everyone’s livelihood, and avoiding wrongful deeds.”

item.title: To seize when favorable, and to defend when unfavorable.
item.description: Before ascending the throne, Zhu’s forces were always the “Army of Benevolence and Righteousness” (Renyi Zhi Shi), and Zhu himself was always a model of practicing the “King’s Way” (Wang Dao). Consequently, the people willingly submitted their hearts and allegiance. Who would have thought that after conquering the realm and incorporating the entire populace into his cage, he would transform from being generous and benevolent to being harsh and cruel, raising the whip and the butcher’s knife to slaughter the world, massacring meritorious officials, and becoming a demonic king that made everyone tremble with fear? In fact, it was not Zhu Yuanzhang’s nature that changed, but the circumstances. Before ascending the throne, he sought support from various social classes; he needed to gain their backing. After ascending the throne, the common people had become the cattle and sheep under his pastoral care, and naturally, he was happy to command them forward with the butcher’s knife and the whip.

item.title: The Significance of Work: Human Transformation from Prehistory to the Future
item.description: Work is the essence of human life, but it is not the purpose of human life. The author argues that from the moment humans appeared on Earth, they have had to engage in labor to acquire resources and energy, thereby sustaining survival and reproduction. However, work is not the sole meaning of human existence; humans also have other needs and pursuits, such as leisure, entertainment, social interaction, and creativity. The author calls on us not to treat work as a religion (or faith), but rather as a means to better enjoy life.
item.content:encoded:
Work is the essence of human life, but it is not the purpose of human life. The author argues that from the moment humans appeared on Earth, they have had to engage in labor to acquire resources and energy, thereby sustaining survival and reproduction. However, work is not the sole meaning of human existence; humans also have other needs and pursuits, such as leisure, entertainment, social interaction, and creativity. The author calls on us not to treat work as a religion (or faith), but rather as a means to better enjoy life.

The form and meaning of work change as human civilization evolves. The author traces the historical transformation of human labor, from primitive society, agricultural society, industrial society, to modern society. He points out that different social forms and economic systems have different definitions and requirements for work. In primitive society, people did not have the concept of “work”; they simply labored to meet basic survival needs. In agricultural society, people began to settle down and cultivate land, forming land ownership and class systems. In industrial society, people were alienated into “tool people” (or “cogs in the machine”), working tirelessly for economic growth. In modern society, people have greater expectations and challenges regarding work, hoping to gain a sense of value and achievement through it.

Scarcity economics is the root cause of people’s overworking. The author believes that the “scarcity mindset” prevalent in modern society makes people worry that resources are insufficient, thus striving hard to work to acquire more wealth and material goods. However, this mindset ignores that human demand for resources is finite, and resources themselves are not fixed or unchanging. The author proposes the concept of “Abundance Economics” (or “Sufficiency Economics”), arguing that humans should learn from primitive society how to control desires, be content with existing resources, and expand the availability of resources through innovation and collaboration.

Automation technology will bring new opportunities and challenges to humanity. The author predicts that in the future, robots will replace humans in performing most repetitive and low-skilled jobs, which will lead humans to face crises of unemployment and uselessness. But at the same time, this will also bring new possibilities to humanity, giving people more time and space to develop fields they are interested in and skilled at, and creating more valuable and meaningful work. The author suggests that we should rethink the question of “what makes us human,” and transition from being “tool people” to being “Human Beings.”

item.title: A little insight from Waterdrop
item.description:
Suidi Chou is listed in the US.

Prospectus

Prospectus link: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1823986/000119312521154899/d95574d424b4.htm#rom95574_23

Core Content

  1. Profitability Status: This company, which occupies the highest moral ground, earned 14.4 billion RMB in 2020 alone, averaging 7,300 RMB per patient.
  2. Donation Status: As of December 31, 2020, over 340 million people have donated to more than 1.7 million patients through Suidi Medical Crowdfunding, accumulating over 37 billion RMB. The average donation per person is 100 RMB, and the average amount received per patient is 21,000 RMB. However, the actual amount received by patients may be less because the company needs to generate profit.
  3. Tencent’s Stake: Tencent currently holds a beneficial ownership stake of 22.1% in Suidi Chou.
  4. Tencent’s Revenue: In 2020, Tencent earned a total of 210 million RMB from Suidi Chou through payment processing fees, advertising, and marketing fees.

Personal Reflection

Every company aims for profit, no matter how noble its banner may be. The world itself is extremely cruel.

item.title: Every sentence is countless pitfalls that have been stepped into.
item.description: 1. Many people’s correct decisions come to an end without a clear outcome: Asking someone who has only ridden a bicycle, “Is Li Auto worth buying?” Asking someone who has never profited from equity investment, “Should you become a Meihua LP?”… Often, the right or wrong decision is determined by the person you consult. One way of giving bad advice is by saying, “It’s for your own good.” When encountering people inferior to you, you must firmly hold your beliefs. When encountering people similar to you, you must doubt your beliefs. When encountering people superior to you, you must negate your beliefs.
item.content:encoded:
1. Many people’s correct decisions come to an end without a clear outcome: Asking someone who has only ridden a bicycle, “Is Li Auto worth buying?” Asking someone who has never profited from equity investment, “Should you become a Meihua LP?”… Often, the right or wrong decision is determined by the person you consult. One way of giving bad advice is by saying, “It’s for your own good.” When encountering people inferior to you, you must firmly hold your beliefs. When encountering people similar to you, you must doubt your beliefs. When encountering people superior to you, you must negate your beliefs.

  2. The only true asset a person possesses is time. The only important strategy is how you use your time. For valuable things, don’t worry about the price; for worthless things, don’t waste time. Whether your decision-making is based on a price mindset or a value mindset will result in vastly different outcomes. Entrepreneurship is like building with LEGOs; time is often spent not on studying the blueprints, but on searching for the pieces. The three things founders must always focus on are: finding people, finding money, and finding direction.

  3. If an entrepreneur does not thoroughly reflect on a lesson, that lesson will be repeated over and over until you completely learn it. People teach people—a hundred times you might not learn it; things teach people—once you will learn it. What convinces a person is not preaching, but a firm, unyielding stance (a “South Wall”).

  4. The opportunity for the poor to turn their fortunes around is placing a heavy stake. If you don’t have the quantity of chips, you must have the multiples; betting evenly is unlikely to lead to a turnaround. Your heavy stakes include money, time, energy, and loyalty. The so-called “first pot of gold” is the amount that allows you to climb the first step. This society is both realistic and cruel; money flows toward those who don’t lack it, and hardship is left for those who can endure it.

  5. Many people’s lives are better than before, but they haven’t become as happy as they imagined. Human happiness is determined in three layers: the first by the senses, the second by dopamine, and the third by endorphins. Most people have the first layer, but most people lack the third. What truly determines the degree of a person’s happiness is how much dopamine is secreted in the second layer. From a dopamine perspective, having existing stock is boring; only gaining increments is interesting. Don’t rely on old capital; establish new achievements. Only with increments will there be dopamine, and only then will there be more happiness. For an investor, a cross-industry stand-up comedy show is an increment.

  6. “Being the least wrong” is a game: “If the level is equivalent, be the one who makes the fewest mistakes.” Similarly, entrepreneurship is a game where, if the strategy and tactics are clear, you are the one who is more efficient or more frugal. Among the new car powerhouses, Li Auto makes the fewest mistakes in the same areas, which wins it a large majority.

  7. An entrepreneur’s evolution requires leaving the comfort zone and entering the adaptation zone. Whoever suffers, changes; whoever changes, adapts; whoever adapts, benefits. The most effective way to leave the comfort zone is to take others as a mirror to reflect your own problems. Ordinary people like to hear pleasant words, just as children like to eat candy—sweet but useless. Experts like to hear unpleasant words, just as adults like to drink tea—bitter but detoxifying.

  8. Don’t pull people onto the entrepreneurial path; instead, attract those who need you on the entrepreneurial path. If you pull people into entrepreneurship, you must make a promise. A promise gives certainty, and certainty triggers laziness and bad behavior.

  9. Smart people find fools as opponents and experts as friends. This is contrary to human nature, but conforms to common sense. Dumb people find experts as opponents and fools as friends. This conforms to human nature, but violates common sense.

  10. A person has three lives: one at birth, one when mental power emerges, and one when cognitive awakening occurs. Mental power and cognition are the Governing and Conception Meridians of the entrepreneur; only by opening them can one truly be invincible. Success without the growth of mental power and cognition is more terrifying than failure, because eventually, time will revert luck-driven success back to its original state. Climbing the social ladder is difficult; falling requires only a very short time.

  11. Humans are naturally double-standard animals. Understanding the double standards of others and overcoming one’s own double standards is a lifelong cultivation—it is a painful spiritual discipline that distinguishes whether a person can truly be objective, honest, and empathetic.

  12. Charlie Munger believes there are 5 items for a happy life:

  • Don’t overconsume; don’t exceed your capacity.
  • Engage in prudent investment.
  • Stay away from toxic people and toxic activities.
  • Maintain lifelong learning.
  • Do more things that involve delayed gratification.

Otherwise, you will need to possess extremely good luck! The master believes that even ordinary things contain subtle complexities. Most people ultimately expect to have extremely good luck, spending time burning incense and praying to Buddha, choosing to enter the temple in evolution and business.

  1. Money that is raised is easily spent; only money earned in the market is worth spending. A first-class entrepreneur’s ability to make money is always far greater than their ability to raise money. 95% of founders’ spending ability must be honed through painful experiences; when you don’t know how to spend, being frugal is very important. Many founders spend money on the back of the knife, or even the hilt, meaning they haven’t spent it on the blade itself.

  2. That’s just how humans are. Even if barely, as long as you are slightly ahead of the opponent in some aspect, a state of flow will emerge, and you can even exert 120% or 150% of your power. You must grit your teeth and insist on leading, fully utilizing the “Great Tree Principle”: in a forest, the taller the tree, the more sunlight it receives. Through photosynthesis, the tree grows faster.

  3. In any company, fence-sitters and opportunists are the majority. When you are struggling or making mistakes, it is normal for them to remain neutral and observe. If you use a single, absolute loyalty-driven value system, you will push them toward your side as your opponents.

  4. The unwritten rules of entrepreneurial socializing are: only screen, don’t educate. Changing others is a huge internal drain; changing yourself is growth. Both favorable circumstances and adversity are reflections of the inner self. If you cling to them, if your heart is moved, they are adversity for you; if you let go, if your heart is still, everything is favorable.

  5. Moving toward the high places means moving toward a higher dimension, not just to gain more ability, but to acquire more information. In a higher dimension, the speed, density, and accuracy of information you possess are completely different; it becomes your cognitive depth. With cognitive depth, you can down-dimension, achieve compatibility, and serve the users you can serve—this is the logic of making money.

  6. “True light is not the absence of darkness, but the state of never being obscured by darkness. A true hero is not the absence of humble sentiment, but the state of never being subjugated by humble sentiment.” — A passage I deeply appreciate.

item.title: If you can’t decide, the answer is no.
item.description: In a world brimming with endless options, making decisions on major life choices can be overwhelming. The article suggests that if you find yourself unable to decide, it's often a sign that the answer is no, emphasizing the importance of clarity and decisiveness in our choice-rich society.
item.content:encoded:
Making Decisions in a World of Endless Options

Common Life Questions

  • Should I marry this person?
  • Should I take this job?
  • Should I buy this house?
  • Should I move to this city?
  • Should I go into business with this person?

The Answer When You Can’t Decide

If you cannot decide, the answer is no. The reason is that modern society is full of options. There are countless choices available.

We live on a planet of seven billion people, and we are connected to everyone via the internet. There are hundreds of thousands of careers available to you. With so many choices, it’s essential to be clear and decisive.

The Power of Compound Interest in the Intellectual Domain

In the intellectual domain, compound interest rules.

When you look at a business with one hundred users growing at a compound rate of 20 percent per month, it can very quickly scale up to having millions of users. Sometimes, even the founders of these companies are surprised by how large their businesses grow.

item.title: The Art of Communication: The Power of Questions
item.description: Exploring how to improve communication by asking questions, rather than forcing others to accept your viewpoint. A simple 'why' can change the direction of the conversation.
item.content:encoded:
Asking someone a question is giving them a chance to speak

The Cycle of Refusal and Explanation

When someone refuses to do something for us, our first reaction is usually to explain to them why they should accept our proposal. If the other party chooses not to concede, we often continue to explain, or present more arguments. We try to force others to accept through our own explanations, and the other party is doing the same thing. This is like a conversation between two deaf people: “No, because…”, “Yes, because…”, “No, because…”, “Yes, because…”, endlessly.

The Simple Word to Change the Dynamic

In fact, a simple word can turn this situation around—“Why.”

item.title: Listening to Others' Perspectives: Uncovering the Gold Mine in Dissenting Views
item.description: The article emphasized the importance of showing interest in others' perspectives during communication, and suggested that when faced with rejection, we should sincerely inquire about the reason to obtain valuable information.
item.content:encoded:
We are always eager to explain to others why they are wrong, but what we should actually be doing is showing interest in their opinions, and this also aligns with our own interests.

When others reject one of your proposals, you first need to show interest in the reasons behind it, and your attitude should be as sincere as possible. You can ask, “Why do you disagree?” (or “Why don’t you agree?”), and then listen carefully to their answer. Their answer is like a gold mine, containing many pieces of information worth pondering and utilizing. This is the secret.

item.title: I am you!
item.description: This article introduces six steps to avoid conflict escalation in communication, including calming one's own and others' emotions, understanding the other party's perspective, confirming understanding through restatement (or paraphrasing), using parallel phrasing to express personal views, and collaboratively finding solutions.
item.content:encoded:
Avoid getting caught in the cycle of explanation, threats, and personal attacks.

Step 1

Calm Your Own Emotions When we feel the impulse to attack the other person internally, we need to try our best to suppress it. For example, we can achieve this through several methods mentioned in the story: · Correcting misjudgments of facts; · Distracting yourself through deep breathing; · Or simply holding back the fist you want to throw; · Or any other method that might work. Every time you feel this impulse flare up during communication with someone, you need to review this step in your mind. Completing this step only takes a few seconds, and it is probably the hardest, yet most important, step. If you don’t have the impulse to attack the other person, that’s naturally even better. You can proceed directly to the next step.

Step 2

Calm the Other Person’s Emotions If the person you are talking to remains calm, it’s easy, and you can skip this step directly. But what if the other person is not calm? The answer is “do almost nothing,” or rather, “do almost nothing.” Especially don’t say to the other person, “Calm down!” or “Getting angry is useless!” At this time, you should follow the principle of “not contradicting, not judging.” Specifically, how do you achieve this? You can reply to the other person using words like “agree,” “okay,” “yes,” or “that’s right.” These words can convey the message to the other person: “What you are saying, and the way you choose to say it, naturally makes sense to you. I am willing to discuss this…”

Step 2: Calm the Other Person’s Emotions If the person you are talking to remains calm, it’s easy, and you can skip this step directly. But what if the other person is not calm? The answer is “do almost nothing,” or rather, “do almost nothing.” Especially don’t say to the other person, “Calm down!” or “Getting angry is useless!” At this time, you should follow the principle of “not contradicting, not judging.” Specifically, how do you achieve this? You can reply to the other person using words like “agree,” “okay,” “yes,” or “that’s right.” These words can convey the message to the other person: “What you are saying, and the way you choose to say it, naturally makes sense to you. I am willing to discuss this problem.”

By doing this, you will achieve an astonishing effect: the other person’s emotions will initially fluctuate, but then they will gradually stabilize until they slowly calm down. Achieving this step only requires the moment you say, “I agree.” If you successfully control your own emotions and successfully calm the other person’s emotions, you can proceed to the next step.

Step 3

Try to Understand Others Rather Than Letting Others Be Understood How do you achieve this step? The simplest method is “asking the other person questions.” The most effective question is: “Why do you disagree with my point of view?” After that, you must listen to their answer and try to look at the issue from their perspective, even putting yourself in their shoes and considering their interests. Strive to understand and accept others’ viewpoints, rather than imposing your own viewpoint on them. You must learn to find “consensus” between both parties in the words they use when explaining, and happily accept the other person’s viewpoint. This is a prerequisite for both parties reaching “consensus.” At this time, you should focus more on others’ “interests” (or “selfishness”): make yourself consider the other person’s interests more! Once you understand the other person’s thoughts, the solution will reveal itself, and the disagreement will be resolved easily. But usually, achieving this is not enough; you need to continue to complete the next step…

Step 4

By Restating the Other Person’s Words to Let Them Understand “That You Have Understood Their Viewpoint” If you want others to listen to your viewpoint, you first need them to speak. Then, use your own words to recount the viewpoint of the other person that you have understood. After that, ask the other person, “Did I get it right?” This will yield an unexpected magical effect—the other person will raise their eyebrows, show a satisfied smile, and exclaim, “That’s right!” Then they will fall silent and listen to you speak. Restating has two benefits: First, you can check whether you truly understood the other person’s viewpoint; Second, it lets your conversational partner know that they have been understood, thereby dispelling the thought of continuing the argument. However, there is a prerequisite for achieving this step—don’t let your previous efforts go down the drain just because you used the wrong word. This word is the keyword for the next step. The use of this word is also an art.

Step 5

Use Parallel Conjunctions to Present Your Viewpoint, Rather Than Pitting Two Opposing Views Against Each Other How do you achieve this? You can use the following words, for example: “As for me,” “For me,” “At the same time,” “From my perspective,” etc., instead of the extremely stiff “That’s right, but…” Then, after both parties have clearly stated the other person’s viewpoint, ask yourself, “How can the other person’s needs be met while simultaneously achieving my own goals?” By doing so, you can utilize the intelligence of both parties to seek a solution. Next, we begin to enter the sixth step.

Step 6

Propose Solutions Using Possible Win-Win Scenarios If we cannot find a feasible solution ourselves, try asking others if they have any good ideas. Then, we can discuss it together. If we cannot find any win-win method, we can use a compromise approach to solve the problem. People are often willing to accept a compromise because it at least establishes a friendly cooperative relationship. So, what if even a compromise solution doesn’t exist? This situation is very rare, but not impossible. At this time, you can negotiate with the other person and spend time together discussing possible ways out. Even if a solution is not ultimately found, at least a good relationship is maintained. And this positive relationship is crucial for achieving future collaboration.

item.title: 10 Principles of Economics
item.description:
1. People face trade-offs.
  2. The cost of some things is what you give up to get them.
  3. Rational people consider marginal quantities.
  4. People react to incentives when they trade with each other.
  5. Trade can make everyone better off.
  6. The market is usually a good way to organize economic activity.
  7. Government sometimes can improve market outcomes and how the entire economy runs.
  8. A country’s standard of living depends on its ability to produce goods and services.
  9. When the government issues too much currency, prices rise.
  10. Society faces the short-run trade-off between inflation and unemployment.

The more desire I have for something to work out a certain way, the less likely I am to see the truth. Especially in business, if something isn’t going well, I try to acknowledge it publicly and I try to acknowledge it publicly in front of my co-founders and friends and co-workers. Then, I’m not hiding it from anybody else. If I’m not hiding it from anybody, I’m not going to delude myself from what’s actually going on.

item.title: Tips for Comment Traffic (or Small Tricks for Comment Traffic)
item.description:
Comment seeding/driving traffic (评论引流) can be traced back to the blog era, where people would mass-comment on other websites. The username and the comment content served as advertisements. By commenting on hundreds or thousands of websites, one could continuously bring in a steady stream of traffic.

A well-known expert in the blogger community, Lu Songsong, insisted on commenting under various blog posts back then, which provided significant help to his later traffic and fame.
item.content:encoded:
Comment seeding/driving traffic (评论引流) can be traced back to the blog era, where people would mass-comment on other websites. The username and the comment content served as advertisements. By commenting on hundreds or thousands of websites, one could continuously bring in a steady stream of traffic.

A well-known expert in the blogger community, Lu Songsong, insisted on commenting under various blog posts back then, which provided significant help to his later traffic and fame.

In the era of self-media (self-publishing/personal branding), this method is still effective, and the key is its simplicity—anyone can do it.

Taking the popular low-cost online courses of recent years as an example: Register a D Account (D 音号), change the username to your business name, and ensure the username and avatar are enticing—making people want to click immediately. Pre-follow several hundred knowledge bloggers, and whenever they publish content, comment on it first.

Don’t post advertisements, as they might be deleted. The comment content can simply follow a template. When commenting on knowledge-based bloggers, you can use phrases like: “Got it,” “This is truly useful, thanks for sharing,” “Nice, saved it,” etc.

For an ordinary video, a baseline view count of three to five hundred is standard, but viral hits reaching tens to millions of views are also common. With your username and avatar exposed countless times, some people will inevitably click on them. By posting business-related videos and leaving your personal WeChat in the signature, people will add you as a friend daily, resulting in a very stable conversion rate.

The specific steps for beginners are as follows:

  1. Find a niche industry that has high conversion rates, is a necessity (high demand), and has a wide market.
  2. Organize relevant materials.
  3. Register a D Account, modify the username and avatar, post a few business-related videos, and use the signature to guide people to add your WeChat.
  4. Follow 100+ quality peers and comment blindly—the more the better.

item.title: What was your figure where you thought you were financially safe?
item.description:
The punishment for the love of money is delivered at the same time as the money. As you make money, you just want even more, and you become paranoid and fearful of losing what you do have. There’s no free lunch.
You make money to solve your money and material problems. I think the best way to stay away from this constant love of money is to not upgrade your lifestyle as you make money. It’s very easy to keep upgrading your lifestyle as you make money. But if you can hold your lifestyle fixed and hopefully make your money in giant lump sums as opposed to a trickle at a time, you won’t have time to upgrade your lifestyle. You may get so far ahead you actually become financially free.

item.title: Low intelligence isn't a bad thing; it's actually a quality user.
item.description:
Tycoons pursue high quality and are hard to fool. Middle class pursues cost-effectiveness and is meticulous/penny-pinching. Idiots act on instinct and are easily fooled.

Instinct includes: seeking cheap deals, emotional reactions, fear of missing out (FOMO), love of getting a bargain…

Live streaming e-commerce primarily relies on short video traffic generation.

What kind of short video is more attractive?

Bankruptcy clearance sales, middle-aged people shedding tears… This perfectly matches the greed for cheap deals and emotionality of the lower class.
item.content:encoded:
Tycoons pursue high quality and are hard to fool. Middle class pursues cost-effectiveness and is meticulous/penny-pinching. Idiots act on instinct and are easily fooled.

Instinct includes: seeking cheap deals, emotional reactions, fear of missing out (FOMO), love of getting a bargain…

Live streaming e-commerce primarily relies on short video traffic generation.

What kind of short video is more attractive?

Bankruptcy clearance sales, middle-aged people shedding tears… This perfectly matches the greed for cheap deals and emotionality of the lower class.

Recently, my brother has been scrolling through short videos and seeing many similar videos. The tactics are all the same: “Business can’t go on,” “Bankrupt,” “Loss-making clearance sale.”

These videos with the same tactics are posted repeatedly, grinding the intelligence of the viewers into the ground.

Through short videos, driving traffic to the live stream room works extremely well.

If the live streaming is proficient, you can also run paid traffic (ad spend). If the return on investment (ROI) is greater than 1, you can amplify the operation, and the returns will be considerable.

If the ROI is even, you aren’t losing; at least you gain a fan. If the ROI is slightly negative, as long as the number of fans increases significantly, you still aren’t losing.

Setting up the live stream room at zero cost: Use a green screen setup and find material from a book wholesale supplier to use as the video background.

There is absolutely no technical complexity throughout the process; OBS + Live Companion is enough to handle it.

The product sources for the live stream room are very simple; you can find them directly from curated alliances—zero cost, zero inventory, earning commissions.

Many of the books are priced like cabbage (very cheap), making the traffic generation effect excellent.

  1. Sellers, in order to boost sales and have more people help sell the goods, will offer low prices to drive volume. This is a standard operation.

  2. When you enter the product page, you will find packages at different prices. The low price is the traffic driver, and the high price is the profit driver. As long as enough people buy, the profit from the high-priced items is enough to cover the losses from the low-priced items, and there will still be a surplus.

Use “brain-dead” videos to attract “brain-dead” viewers into the live stream room. Use paid traffic to boost the live stream room’s data. Use “cabbage-priced” products to attract “leeks” (easy targets/consumers). Use profit-driven products to increase revenue.

With a live stream room like this, how will the sales be?

Monthly sales of 50,000 units+

The overall operational framework is just like this; there is no technical complexity.

One background image, randomly copy some popular inspirational quotes, and you can create a video in minutes.

Even these “lame/trash” videos can get over ten thousand views….

The only drawback is that 97% of the traffic is system-pushed. Once you post content from other fields, the views immediately drop to a few hundred.

item.title: Don’t play zero-sum games
item.description: The article explores the dynamics between wealth creation as a positive-sum game and status as a zero-sum game, highlighting how some people attack wealth creation in pursuit of status.
item.content:encoded:
The business world has many people playing zero sum games and a few playing positive sum games searching for each other in the crowd.

Wealth creation is an evolutionarily recent positive-sum game. Status is an old zero-sum game. Those attacking wealth creation are often just seeking status.

The more you’re going to do it for yourself. You’re going to do it in a way you’re good at, and you’re going to stick with it. The people around you will see the quality of your work is higher.

item.title: Forget rich versus poor, white-collar versus blue. It’s now leveraged versus un-leveraged.
item.description: The most interesting and the most important form of leverage is the idea of products that have no marginal cost of replication. This is the new form of leverage. This was only invented in the last few hundred years. It started with the printing press. It accelerated with broadcast media, and now it’s really blown up with the internet and with coding. Now, you can multiply your efforts without involving other humans and without needing money from other humans.

item.title: There are three broad classes of leverage
item.description: One form of leverage is labor—other humans working for you. It is the oldest form of leverage, and actually not a great one in the modern world. [1] I would argue this is the worst form of leverage that you could possibly use. Managing other people is incredibly messy. It requires tremendous leadership skills. You’re one short hop from a mutiny or getting eaten or torn apart by the mob. [78] Money is good as a form of leverage. It means every time you make a decision, you multiply it with money. [1] Capital is a trickier form of leverage to use. It’s more modern. It’s the one that people have used to get fabulously wealthy in the last century. It’s probably been the dominant form of leverage in the last century. You can see this by looking for the richest people. It’s bankers, politicians in corrupt countries who print money, essentially people who move large amounts of money around. If you look at the top of very large companies, outside of technology companies, in many, many large old companies, the CEO job is really a financial job. It scales very, very well. If you get good at managing capital, you can manage more and more capital much more easily than you can manage more and more people. The final form of leverage is brand new—the most democratic form. It is: “products with no marginal cost of replication.” This includes books, media, movies, and code. Code is probably the most powerful form of permissionless leverage. All you need is a computer—you don’t need anyone’s permission.

item.title: The leverage for ordinary people
item.description: Probably the most interesting thing to keep in mind about new forms of leverage is they are permissionless. They don’t require somebody else’s permission for you to use them or succeed. For labor leverage, somebody has to decide to follow you. For capital leverage, somebody has to give you money to invest or to turn into a product.

item.description:
Compound interest is a very powerful concept. Compound interest applies to more than just compounding capital. Compounding capital is just the beginning.
Compound interest also happens in your reputation.
If you have a sterling reputation and you keep building it for decades upon decades, people will notice.
Your reputation will literally end up being thousands or tens of thousands of times more valuable than somebody else who was very talented but is not keeping the compound interest in reputation going.

item.title: Wealth is assets that earn while you sleep.
item.description:
Wealth is the thing you want. Wealth is
the factory, the robots, cranking out things. Wealth is the computer program that’s running at night, serving other customers. Wealth is even money in the bank that is being reinvested into other assets, and into other businesses. Even a house can be a form of wealth, because you can rent it out, although that’s probably a lower productivity use of land than some commercial enterprise.
So, my definition of wealth is much more businesses and assets that can earn while you sleep.

item.title: Never use short-term solutions to deal with long-term problems.
item.description: I absolutely cannot let people think I am stingy. So, I frequently invite friends to restaurants; I also need a luxury car to display my status; furthermore, I must pay some other expenses—taxes. Finally, I have to turn to this great invention: the credit card. With a credit card, I don’t have to pay myself; the people at the credit card company will help me pay, at least temporarily… After that, I heard someone say, “He is truly a winner in life; he is living a first-class life.” I was living a first-class life: not drinking sparkling wine—only champagne; not eating a steak—only prime tenderloin. I wanted to live like a rich person in a futuristic world. And soon, the past began to constantly bother me in the form of bills, collection letters, and high loan interest rates. As a high-performing, high-income salesperson, I was always able to get a new credit card. So, I started making revolving payments, meaning I would get a new credit card and then use the new card to pay off the bill of the old credit card. Just like that, I spiraled into a downward financial state.

item.title: Never use your principal.
item.description:
First, we must clarify an important principle: You must never kill your “goose.” You also cannot cut it into small pieces. You absolutely cannot touch your principal.

All your dreams can be fulfilled with the help of the golden eggs. This also means that your golden eggs must be large enough to support your dreams.

For example, you want to buy a house. If you have already achieved financial freedom, then you can undoubtedly use your assets for payment. But in this way, your assets will diminish, which is naturally what you don’t want to see. Therefore, you should adopt the method of installment payments to acquire all the big items, because your monthly interest will be completely sufficient to cover it.

item.title: Your investment strategy
item.description: Achieving financial security requires that the most important standard—the availability of money—is met. You must have a daily income. Therefore, it is best to put your money in a safe or invest it in a cash fund. You should not take risks until you achieve financial security. Consequently, you should choose low-risk investment projects. However, even so, you must pay attention to managing potential risks. Never put all your money into a single investment project, even if “all your funds” only total 1,000 Euros. Remember, managing risk means increasing the opportunity for profit. Before achieving financial security, keep financial safety at the center. You should tolerate a low profit rate and keep some cash in a bank savings account. If you still want to invest, I recommend a deposit plan.
item.content:encoded:
Achieving financial security requires that the most important standard—the availability of money—is met. You must have a daily income. Therefore, it is best to put your money in a safe or invest it in a cash fund. You should not take risks until you achieve financial security. Consequently, you should choose low-risk investment projects. However, even so, you must pay attention to managing potential risks. Never put all your money into a single investment project, even if “all your funds” only total 1,000 Euros. Remember, managing risk means increasing the opportunity for profit. Before achieving financial security, keep financial safety at the center. You should tolerate a low profit rate and keep some cash in a bank savings account. If you still want to invest, I recommend a deposit plan.

The 40:40:20 Principle Guarantees Financial Security To achieve financial security, you must change the allocation ratio of your money. Although most of the money must still be put into low-risk investments, you can allocate 40% to moderately risky investments. If you consistently hold this money without using it, the risk will be greatly reduced through the effect of “average cost return.” The remaining 20% can be invested in high-risk projects, which involves speculative funds such as emerging market funds or national funds, as well as all special funds and corporate participation funds. The risk of these funds can also be reduced over time through the effect of “average cost return.” On the other hand, your probability of profit is also extremely high. One important point is: you absolutely cannot put the money used to guarantee your financial security into high-risk or speculative projects. You must not touch this money. The investments you make must guarantee that your financial security is never affected.

item.title: Little Dog Money Summary
item.description: Some people who read this book cannot take in what you say, so there is no change. Others, after reading it, begin to be smart about geography and finance, and they will have a happier and richer life.
item.content:encoded:
The Foundation of Wealth Building

Financial freedom is a goal that anyone today can achieve, of course, this requires us to have the courage to pursue the life we truly desire. As a famous saying goes: “It is not the difficulty that makes us give up, but rather that we give up, which makes it seem so difficult.”

If we keep the laws of money in mind, we will find that our financial situation is steadily improving. Nothing can stop a mindset that aligns with the times. This also applies to everyone’s life. Nothing can stop us from enjoying the right we are born with—wealth. A life of dignity and financial comfort aligns with our natural laws. As long as we don’t give up, nothing can prevent us from reaching this goal.

Making a Dream Album

To achieve financial freedom, we must have motivation. Therefore, the first thing we must do is think up 10 reasons (wishes) why we want to become wealthy, and write them down. This will be the driving force for our actions.

Next, from these 10 reasons for wanting to become wealthy, select the top 3 most important ones. Don’t set yourself too many goals, as that might be unrealistic. Human desires are endless, and we need to distinguish between primary and secondary, determining which are the most important goals. After setting the goals, we must find ways to achieve them.

One method taught by Qianqian to Jia is to use a Dream Album and a Dream Piggy Bank: the Dream Album is used to collect photos related to your wishes, and you paste them into the album.

Looking at the Album Daily

The act of thinking through pictures and imagining the scenarios where you achieve your wishes is called “visualization.”

Preparing a Dream Piggy Bank

Prepare a piggy bank for each dream, and write your dream on it. Once the piggy bank is ready, save every penny you save into it.

When Jia doubted whether the Dream Album would be effective, Qianqian said: “Curiosity is good, but it must never hinder your actions. Too many people hesitate in their actions simply because they feel they haven’t fully understood the matter. Putting it into practice is much more useful than pure thinking.”

When we question whether this fantasy is a “pipe dream,” we need to know that “successful people are successful because they always dream of the day they succeed, constantly imagining the situation when they have achieved their dreams. Of course, people cannot remain stuck in dreams.”

“Learning is the process of recognizing new concepts and new ideas. If people always consider problems using the same way of thinking, they will always get the same results. Don’t jump to conclusions before you have done it.”

People without imagination find it difficult to achieve great things. The more effort we put into something, the greater the possibility of success. But most people put their energy into things they don’t like, instead of imagining what they hope to gain.

Don’t approach it with a “let’s try” mindset; take concrete action! If you only approach it with a “let’s try” mindset, it will only end in failure, and we will achieve nothing. ‘Trying’ is merely an excuse; before we even try, we have already prepared an escape route for ourselves. There is no option to ’try’; there are only two choices—to do it or not to do it."

Success Journal

When we do something, we need sufficient self-confidence. Our level of confidence determines whether we believe in our ability and whether we believe in ourselves. If we fundamentally don’t believe we can do it, we won’t even start, and if we don’t start, we will gain nothing."

Therefore, we need to keep a “Success Journal.” The “Success Journal” is similar to a diary; record all the things you have successfully done in it, writing down at least 5 personal achievements every day, no matter how small. The main purpose of doing this is to help us boost our self-confidence.

At the beginning, we might feel it’s difficult, and we might ask ourselves, “Can this or that thing really be counted as an achievement?” In this case, our answer should be affirmative. Being overly confident is much better than being insufficiently confident."

When we encounter problems:

a. Still stick to your idea Everyone can do this when things are normal. It is only when true difficulties arise that the difference becomes clear. Only a few people can firmly implement their plans. Very successful people even have the ability to perform exceptionally when things are at their most difficult.

b. When progress is smooth Even when everything is progressing very smoothly, you must firmly stick to your plan.

c. The 72-Hour Rule When we decide to do something, we must complete it within 72 hours, otherwise, we are likely to never do it again."

“How much money a person earns is linked to their self-confidence. Furthermore, whether their experiences are focused within their scope of ability or placed outside of what they can achieve is also very important. Without a Success Journal, we won’t think about in which areas we are suited to earn money.”

Often, our inability to act stems from the psychology of fear. Fear always appears when we imagine how things might go wrong. The more we think about the possibility of failure, the more afraid we become. But when we look at our Success Journal, we notice the successful things, and naturally, we think about how to do them."

Earning and Saving Money

When Qianqian encouraged Jia to bravely earn money, she told the story of a young boy named Darryl. Darryl became a millionaire at the age of 17 through personal effort, making him a role model for Jia.

In Darryl’s story, a businessman gave Darryl (Jia’s role model) advice on earning money:

  1. Figure out what you like, and then figure out how to earn money from it.
  2. Solve a problem for others, and you will earn a lot of money;
  3. Focus your energy on what you know, what you can do, and what you possess.
  4. Before buying something, ask yourself, “Is this really necessary?”

Mr. Jin, when guiding Jia not to spend all the money she had immediately, told the story of a goose that lays golden eggs:

A goose raised by a farmer lays a golden egg every day. The farmer was very greedy and hoped the goose would lay at least two golden eggs every day. In a fit of pique, he killed the goose, and from then on, he never received another golden egg. The goose is the principal, and the golden egg is the interest. The farmer’s biggest mistake was not “killing” his “goose.”

Expenditure and income are directly proportional; the higher the income, the higher the expenditure, unless you learn to allocate your assets reasonably and learn to spend within your means.

Advice for Those in Debt:

a. Destroy all credit cards Spending with a credit card costs more than spending with cash.

b. Pay the minimum installment amount within the allowed limit The higher the installment amount, the less living money you have left each month. Often, people underestimate how high their living expenses are, and they might take out new loans to pay off old ones when a large expense occurs.

c. For consumer loans For loans for goods in daily life, such as a TV loan, it is best not to apply for it first. If you do apply, save half of the money remaining after deducting living expenses, and use the other half to pay the consumer loan.

Fund Allocation

The author suggests that we can divide our income into Daily Expenses (10%) + Dream Goals (40%) + Golden Goose Account (50%). This means we can save 50% of our income, and this money should not be easily touched; it is like the goose mentioned earlier that lays golden eggs, allowing money to generate more money.

Of the remaining 50%, besides the 10% needed for daily life, the remaining 40% is saved to achieve the dreams we want, such as buying a phone as a reward for yourself, or going on a trip, etc. This amount is up to you to manage and plan; remember to allocate it reasonably.

Golden Goose: From the story of laying golden eggs, the “goose” refers to the money (savings value), and the “golden egg” refers to the interest.

Never kill your goose, and don’t use all your money to pay off loans, leaving yourself with nothing. Having nothing is not our goal; our goal is to achieve the initial 3 wishes or accumulate the savings.

Passive Income

Investment Tips:

  1. Invest money in a safe place.
  2. Money should lay many “golden eggs” (choose high interest, with the highest dividends coming from stocks).
  3. Investment should be simple and clear, easy to operate.

The 72 Rule:

Divide 72 by the annual profit percentage of the investment, and the resulting number is the number of years required for that money to double.

Divide 72 by a certain inflation rate, and you can find out how many years it will take for the money to lose half its value.

When the market declines, losses only occur when you actually sell the fund.

A fund has an indicator—the Fluctuation Rate (Volatility): a lower fluctuation rate means higher safety and more stable profit growth. Funds generally last 5 to 10 years; the market always has ups and downs, but the overall trend is upward, so you can check the market after 5 or 10 years.

72 / Return Rate = Time to Double 72 / Inflation Rate = Time to Half Value 115 Rule: 115 / Return Rate = Time to Double

Controlling Risk

Cash Reserves are Necessary

You cannot put all your money into stocks or funds; you must reserve some cash to have liquid funds, so that when the stock market declines, you can buy appropriately at the right time. The remaining reserve cash can be invested in short-term income projects, such as daily deposits. Bank passbooks are merely money-swallowing machines; their returns are often less than the losses caused by inflation. Some savings accounts have high interest rates, but they require keeping the cash in the bank for a relatively long time, so the author does not recommend relying solely on bank passbooks.

Qianqian’s Words

Some people who read this book do not absorb what you say, and thus make no changes. Others, after reading it, begin to manage their finances wisely, and they will lead happier and wealthier lives.

item.title: A logical flaw caused by poor arguments (or weak premises)
item.description:
Mr. Willy’s desk is always a mess because he is incompetent. A messy desk indicates a confused mind, which can only mean one thing: he is unfit for his job.

The statement above is actually very simple: “He is incompetent, so his desk is messy; because his desk is messy, he is unable to perform his job.”

Fallacies (or Logical Errors)

1. Appeal to Ignorance (or Argument from Ignorance) When we conclude that something is true simply because it “has not been proven false,” or conclude that it is false simply because it “has not been proven true,” our judgment contains a logical flaw. For example, although no one has found evidence of Atlantis’s existence yet, this does not mean that Atlantis does not exist.
item.content:encoded:
Mr. Willy’s desk is always a mess because he is incompetent. A messy desk indicates a confused mind, which can only mean one thing: he is unfit for his job.

The statement above is actually very simple: “He is incompetent, so his desk is messy; because his desk is messy, he is unable to perform his job.”

Fallacies (or Logical Errors)

1. Appeal to Ignorance (or Argument from Ignorance) When we conclude that something is true simply because it “has not been proven false,” or conclude that it is false simply because it “has not been proven true,” our judgment contains a logical flaw. For example, although no one has found evidence of Atlantis’s existence yet, this does not mean that Atlantis does not exist.

2. Hasty Generalization When we rush to draw a conclusion based on a small sample, we are prone to committing the fallacy of hasty generalization. “I have been to Phoenix three times, and it rained every time, so Phoenix must definitely be a rainy city.” (In fact, Phoenix is a desert-like, dry city.)

“Because none of the interns in the company have complained that the salary is too low, we can confidently say that the interns in the company are all satisfied with their salaries.”

3. Personal Bias When we judge something solely based on personal emotions without considering the actual situation, we are committing the fallacy of personal bias. “How can you consult Sheila about marriage problems? Don’t you know she was once jailed for email fraud?”

4. Poisoning the Well When we judge someone’s words too much based on their background, especially their nationality, race, or gender, our logic goes awry. “How can your words be taken seriously? You are from Sydney, so of course you think Sydney is better than Melbourne.”

5. You’re No Better Off If we reject someone’s viewpoint simply because they made the same mistake we did, our logic also goes awry. Father: “Son, you shouldn’t drink. Alcohol damages the liver; how can you be drunk all the time?” Son: “Dad, aren’t you holding a glass of wine right now?” Although the son’s father is also drinking, this does not mean that his advice to his son is wrong.

6. Red Herring When we try to divert the topic to avoid our own weaknesses during a conversation, we are committing the “Red Herring” fallacy. (Boss to subordinate): “Don’t tell me the salary is too low. When I was your age, I only earned $100 a week.” The fact that the boss earned a low income when young is irrelevant to the current conversation, because the boss’s low income in his youth does not mean the subordinate shouldn’t get a raise.

7. Forcing an Irrelevant Conclusion or Function When we reject a rule or plan because it fails to satisfy some unrelated goal, we are committing this logical error. Pete: “Do you really think studying logic can solve the problems of this world?” Tiffany: “Probably not.” Pete: “Then why are we wasting time studying it?”

8. Wishful Thinking When we assume something is true (or false) simply because we desperately wish it to be so, we are committing the “Wishful Thinking” fallacy. “No matter how our team performed before, we will defeat the reigning champion in the first round. Our players are very confident and are determined to achieve a great victory.”

9. Appeal to Tradition/Seniority When we try to convince an opponent based on factors like seniority or tradition, rather than facts or evidence, we are committing this logical error. “Tim, don’t take the idea of going to Annapolis too seriously! Your family—including your father, brothers, grandfather, uncles, etc.—has always been in the military, and they will continue to be in the service. So, young man, your future is at West Point!”

10. Appeal to Popular Opinion When we accept or support a viewpoint simply because everyone agrees with it, we are committing this logical error. “I am going to vote in favor of the tax amendment. According to a recent public opinion poll, more than two-thirds of registered voters under the age of 25 support the amendment.”

11. Pity (or Appeal to Pity) “Pity” refers to the method of persuading someone by appealing to their sympathy, rather than by presenting factual evidence. (Sheila to John): “You must donate to the orphanage. These children are born without knowing who their biological parents are, let alone having food and shelter.”

item.title: Logical flaw resulting from incorrect assumptions
item.description:
· Either/Or (Dichotomy) Just because there are only two choices presented, one cannot assume that one of them is necessarily correct. Many things are not strictly “either/or” or “black/white.” For example: “Since you don’t support free trade, you must support protectionism!”

· Middle Value (Moderation) Many people prefer to take the middle ground between two choices because it avoids either extreme. This practice is sometimes referred to as the Doctrine of the Mean (or Golden Mean). “The junior high teacher believes that the school should arrange a fixed curriculum schedule. Meanwhile, the parents believe that students should be able to choose their courses freely. Therefore, the best solution is to combine the two.”
item.content:encoded:
· Either/Or (Dichotomy) Just because there are only two choices presented, one cannot assume that one of them is necessarily correct. Many things are not strictly “either/or” or “black/white.” For example: “Since you don’t support free trade, you must support protectionism!”

· Middle Value (Moderation) Many people prefer to take the middle ground between two choices because it avoids either extreme. This practice is sometimes referred to as the Doctrine of the Mean (or Golden Mean). “The junior high teacher believes that the school should arrange a fixed curriculum schedule. Meanwhile, the parents believe that students should be able to choose their courses freely. Therefore, the best solution is to combine the two.”

· Hodgepodge (Amalgamation) Just because you combine locally correct elements does not necessarily result in a correct overall outcome. “Brad is a nice young man, and Janet is an excellent lady; they must be a perfect pair.” Marriage is not as simple as “1+1=2.” Two excellent individuals may not necessarily become a pair of excellent spouses, meaning local correctness does not automatically imply overall correctness.

· Local Error (Partial Error) Just because the whole is correct does not mean that every single part of it is correct. For example, a team may be great, but that does not mean that every player on that team is equally great. “Because the car is heavy, all the parts on the car must be heavy.” Clearly, this statement is not necessarily true!

· Continuity Gap (Continuity Flaw) Sometimes people feel that certain differences are too minuscule to be worth noting, and this is where the continuity gap appears. “Learn one new word every day to improve your vocabulary. Take a medium-sized dictionary and start from the beginning. By learning one new word every day, you will slowly reach the last page. And more importantly, you will learn almost all the important words in English. But how many people can achieve this?”

· Attacking the Point (Attacking the Specifics) Many people believe that an inductive argument is easily refuted simply by finding one exception. For instance, a cinema might claim that children under 18 are not allowed entry, but this does not mean that parents cannot bring in a 7-month-old baby to watch the movie. Student A: “It is well known that smoking shortens human lifespan.” Student B: “Yes, but my great-grandfather smoked a pack a day and is still over 90 years old and doing fine. How should we explain that?” Finding an exception does not mean the induction is flawed—everything has exceptions, but exceptions are always exceptions, merely low-probability events.

· Distortion (Twisting) Distortion refers to deliberately twisting an opponent’s viewpoint in order to achieve the goal of refuting them. Proponent: “The only way to improve the education level of developing countries is to provide more material support, such as textbooks.” Opponent: “Are you suggesting that no matter how many trees you cut down, you still have to print more textbooks?”

· Faulty Analogy (False Analogy) We cannot assume that two things are similar (or dissimilar) in other aspects just because they are similar (or dissimilar) in one or a few aspects. “Speaking of artificial lures, my favorite is the Rapala lure. This summer, every time I used it, I caught many small bass, so I will definitely use it when fishing for trout in the fall.”

· Causal Error (Fallacy of Causation) When we arbitrarily attribute an event to a specific cause, we are committing a causal error. “I heard that rich people work very hard, so I must work hard to become rich.” Indeed, working hard might make a person wealthy (at least financially), but it is only one factor. We cannot arbitrarily assume that hard work alone is sufficient to turn a pauper into a rich person.

· Domino Error (Domino Effect Fallacy) We cannot assume that if one event triggers another, it will necessarily trigger a subsequent series of events. The domino error is sometimes also called the “Chain Reaction Error.” “I don’t oppose providing free food to the homeless, but since we provide free food, we will need to provide free clothes, and then free accommodation. Soon, we will have to provide them with a fixed annual salary.”

· Gambler’s Fallacy When we judge the probability of a future event based on past occurrences—and these two events are completely independent and unrelated—we are committing the Gambler’s Fallacy. (Parents to doctor): “Since we already have three boys, I believe the next one must be a girl.” The result of the last birth has absolutely no bearing on the result of the next birth; it is certain that the probability of the next birth being a boy or a girl is still 50/50.

· Faulty Precision (Misleading Precision) Faulty precision refers to arbitrarily citing numbers that appear precise but are actually baseless in fact to prove one’s point. “In Shakespeare’s time, one in four people disliked Shakespeare’s plays.” The speaker could not possibly obtain such precise data, especially data from the Shakespearean era over four hundred years ago.

item.title: Logical error in the reasoning process
item.description: · Error of Asserting the Conclusion We cannot conclude that “when B is true, A is true” just because “when A is true, B is true.” This error is also called the “Conversion Error.” “Every time I go on vacation, I feel very relaxed. Therefore, when I feel very relaxed, I must be on vacation.” Relaxation during vacation does not mean that relaxation only happens during vacation; I might relax at home, I might relax while eating dinner, I might feel relaxed while chatting with friends… Therefore, the fallacy of the statement above is obvious.
item.content:encoded:
· Error of Asserting the Conclusion We cannot conclude that “when B is true, A is true” just because “when A is true, B is true.” This error is also called the “Conversion Error.” “Every time I go on vacation, I feel very relaxed. Therefore, when I feel very relaxed, I must be on vacation.” Relaxation during vacation does not mean that relaxation only happens during vacation; I might relax at home, I might relax while eating dinner, I might feel relaxed while chatting with friends… Therefore, the fallacy of the statement above is obvious.

· Negation of the Antecedent We cannot conclude that “if A is not true, B is not true” just because “if A is true, B is true.” “Every time it rains, the ground gets wet. Last night it didn’t rain, so the ground cannot be wet.” Without a doubt, many situations can make the ground wet; it doesn’t necessarily have to rain.

item.title: Why risk keeping so much money and gold at home?
item.description: “There are many reasons,” the old lady explained to me, “First, because sometimes I just like holding these things to admire them. I really like gold and banknotes.” I looked at her with slight disagreement, thinking to myself that liking money in this way—I wonder if it’s normal—and she admits it so frankly… But then I recalled that day, when Marcel and I were looking at the things in the box and counting them one by one. How delightful it was when we touched each gold bar! Shouldn’t an old lady enjoy the same sense of happiness when opening a box? Besides, these things belong to her. Mrs. Tao Mu continued, “Second, this money is kept for emergencies. No matter what happens, the things in the box will be enough for me to live on for several years.” “That’s a bit too much, isn’t it!” I said with a laugh. “That depends on how much money you have in total,” Mrs. Tao Mu explained. “If you keep cash at home that is more than 10% of your total assets, then it’s meaningless.” I whistled softly. This old lady must be very wealthy. “Third, I have invested a large portion of the money in stocks, which involves a certain risk. So, it is wise to keep a portion of the money readily available. I can explain this to you in more detail another time.”

item.title: If they didn't have to worry about money, they could live very well.
item.description: To live a happier and more satisfying life, one must change oneself. This has nothing to do with money; money itself neither makes people happy nor brings misfortune. Money is neutral; it is neither good nor bad. Only when money belongs to a specific person will it exert a positive or negative influence on that person. Money can be used for good purposes, or it can be used for bad ones. A happy person will be happier when they have money; conversely, a pessimistic or anxious person will have more worries the more money they possess.

item.title: When in debt, you also need a goose.
item.description:
First, people who are in debt should destroy all their credit cards. This is because most people spend much more when using credit cards than when using cash.

The second piece of advice is that one should repay each loan installment as little as possible. In most cases, they haven’t estimated that living expenses will be so high. When they must purchase a new car or something in the house breaks down, they have to pay for these things by taking out another loan.

When they must purchase a new car or something in the house breaks down, they have to pay for these things by taking out another loan.

Third, half of the money that is not used for living should be saved, and the other half should be used to repay the loan.
