item.title: Money Quotes
item.description:
1. Money has certain secrets and patterns. The prerequisite for understanding these secrets and patterns is that you must genuinely desire them yourself.
  2. If you only approach it with a “let’s try it” mindset, you will ultimately end in failure and achieve nothing.
  3. “Trying” is an excuse. Before you even do it, you have already prepared an escape route for yourself.
  4. If you cannot test it, you only have two choices: do it or don’t do it.
  5. The most critical factor in whether you can earn money is not whether you have a good idea.
  6. How smart you are is not the main reason; the determining factor is your level of confidence.
  7. You must first clarify where your interests lie, and then consider how to earn money through them.
  8. You must do things every day without interruption that are highly significant to your future.
  9. The time you spend on this will not exceed 10 minutes, but those 10 minutes will make everything different.
  10. People who are in debt should cancel all their credit cards.
  11. You should repay loans as much as possible.
  12. You should save half of the money that isn’t used for living, and use the other half to pay off debt.
  13. It is best not to apply for consumer loans at all.
  14. Before borrowing money every time, first ask yourself: “Is this really necessary?” When you set a big goal, it means you must put in much more effort than others.
  15. Poverty makes people even less fortunate.
  16. If I don’t have my “goose,” I always have to work just to earn money.
  17. But once I have a “goose,” my “money will automatically work for me.”
  18. Luck is actually just the result of sufficient preparation combined with hard work.
  19. Money only stays with those who put in the effort for it.
  20. People who acquire unjust wealth through illegal means often feel worse than when they have no money at all.
  21. Fear always appears when we imagine how things might go wrong.
  22. The more we think about the possibility of failure, the more afraid we become.
  23. But when you think toward positive goals, you will not feel fear.
  24. Whenever winter passes, spring comes, followed by summer; after every summer comes autumn, and then winter again—year after year.
  25. Just like the changes in nature, the stock exchange always experiences the changing of seasons, cycling back and forth.
  26. If you don’t do this thing today, you will never know what you are capable of writing after putting some pressure on yourself.
  27. The things a person feels the most proud of are the ones that were the most difficult to achieve.

item.title: But Monica's parents' financial situation is getting better, isn't it?
item.description: Soon, I turned 12. Everything was still the same; we still didn’t go on vacation by the sea. Mom and Dad kept saying that business was affected by the “economic recession.” What they meant was that the domestic economic situation was the root cause of their financial problems. But I had a question: why was my friend Monica’s parents’ financial situation getting better and better, even with the same economic situation?

item.title: It's not trying, but taking action!
item.description: If you only approach things with a “try-it-out” mindset, then you will ultimately end in failure, and you will achieve nothing. Trying is purely an excuse; before you even do it, you have already prepared an escape route for yourself. If you can’t test, you only have two choices—do it or don’t do it. Too many people hesitate when doing things simply because they feel they haven’t fully grasped something. And actually putting it into practice is much smarter than pure thinking.

item.title: The 24 Common Logical Fallacies
item.description:
Distorting Viewpoint

Literal Translation: Straw Man Other Names: Straw Dummy / Misrepresentation

It is the act of distorting an opponent’s arguments to make them easier to attack.

By exaggerating, twisting, or even completely fabricating an opponent’s arguments, one presents their own position as more reasonable. However, sincere and rational debate is destroyed by this form of argumentation, which is essentially fraud.

Example: Xiao Ming says: “The state should invest more funds in the medical and education sectors.” Xiao Liang replies: “That’s terrifying! You actually hate the country so much, that you want to reduce defense spending, leaving our army defenseless and unable to protect the nation.”
item.content:encoded:
Distorting Viewpoint

Literal Translation: Straw Man Other Names: Straw Dummy / Misrepresentation

It is the act of distorting an opponent’s arguments to make them easier to attack.

By exaggerating, twisting, or even completely fabricating an opponent’s arguments, one presents their own position as more reasonable. However, sincere and rational debate is destroyed by this form of argumentation, which is essentially fraud.

Example: Xiao Ming says: “The state should invest more funds in the medical and education sectors.” Xiao Liang replies: “That’s terrifying! You actually hate the country so much, that you want to reduce defense spending, leaving our army defenseless and unable to protect the nation.”

Note: The original English term for this fallacy, “strawman,” literally translates to “straw dummy.” Since a straw dummy is not a real person, it won’t offer any resistance in a fight, and it is very easy to knock down. In the UK, this fallacy is also often called “Aunt Sally.”

Causal Attribution Error

It is concluding that a causal relationship exists between two things, either genuinely existing or hypothetically assumed, based on the association between them.

It is assuming that a causal relationship exists between two things simply because they are associated, or merely because they exist simultaneously. Different things may occur simultaneously or sequentially, but this does not necessarily mean that one is the cause of the other. Sometimes, the association between two things is purely coincidental, and it is even possible that both things share the same cause.

Example: Xiao Ming points to a table and says, “Over the past few centuries, global temperatures have been rising, and at the same time, the number of pirates has been decreasing. Therefore, we can conclude: the existence of pirates lowers global temperatures, and global warming is a hoax.”

Emotional Blackmail (or Emotional Manipulation)

It is substituting genuine, effective arguments with the manipulation of emotions.

Emotional blackmail includes manipulating fear, jealousy, hatred, pity, pride, and so on. There is one very important thing we must know: sometimes a logically sound argument may trigger a strong emotional response. But abandoning logic and relying solely on appeals to emotion to mask the fact that one’s own viewpoint lacks strong evidence will only lead to more problems and fallacies. Every mentally healthy person is influenced by emotions, so emotional blackmail is a very common and effective debate strategy, but fundamentally, it is a flawed and hypocritical way of arguing, and it tends to rationalize the emotional state of the other party in the debate.

Example: Xiao Liang dislikes drinking mutton soup, but his father tells him, “Think about the children in poor African countries who are starving to death, those pitiful kids who can’t eat anything.”

Fallacy Leading to Error (or Fallacious Conclusion)

Literal Translation: Fallacy Fallacy Other Names: Mistaking Error for Error / Assuming Error

It is judging that a conclusion must be wrong simply because the level of argumentation is poor, or because the argument contains errors.

It is not logically sound to assume that a viewpoint must lead to a fallacious conclusion; even incorrect premises can be presented using sound logic. Similarly, it is entirely possible to prove a correct viewpoint using flawed premises in a debate, or to include logical fallacies in the process of argumentation.

Example: Xiao Li discovers that Xiao Hong advocates for a healthy diet merely because some dubious nutritionist claims, “A healthy diet is a popular lifestyle,” which is unreliable. But Xiao Li then concludes, “Therefore, the conclusion that a healthy diet is necessary is wrong, and binge eating every day is fine,” which is also a fallacy.

Slippery Slope

If A happens, then eventually bad thing Z will happen, so we cannot allow A to happen.

The problem is that this form of reasoning avoids discussing the current issue A, instead shifting the focus to the hypothetical extreme assumption Z. Furthermore, there is no evidence to prove that Z will necessarily happen because of A. This fallacy is also a form of emotional blackmail, using fear to undermine the fairness of the current discussion with unverified speculation.

Example: Xiao Qiang asserts that if we allow same-sex marriage, the next thing that will happen is that we will allow incestuous marriage, and even allow humans to marry monkeys or humans to marry cars.

Ad Hominem (Attacking the Person)

It is diminishing an opponent’s argument by attacking their personal character or other personal traits, such as height, appearance, social status, etc.

Ad hominem can be a public, blatant attack, or it can be a subtle implication that the opponent’s character is questionable, thereby discrediting their argument. In an argument, ad hominem often achieves the effect of defeating the opponent without a fight.

Example: Huihui presents undeniable evidence showing that the new tax system is fairer, more reasonable, and worth promoting. Zhuang asks the attendees: “Do you think you should believe anything said by a woman who is unmarried, has a criminal record, and smells like body odor?”

Tu Quoque (You Too)

Responding to criticism by criticizing the critic: To avoid directly addressing the criticism, one turns the accusation back onto the person who raised the criticism.

The original Latin term for this fallacy is tu quoque, meaning “you too (have done it).” This logical fallacy is commonly known as “hypocrisy of the critic.” It is usually a diversionary tactic that allows the party who must defend their argument to shift the focus from themselves back onto the person who raised the criticism.

Example: At the hospital, Xiao Mei points out that Xiao Li’s poor health condition is due to her failure to strictly follow the doctor’s orders. Instead of reflecting on why she didn’t follow the orders, Xiao Li blames Xiao Mei: “Don’t talk about me! You never listened to the doctor’s advice either; you never took your medicine on time!”

Note: In China, this fallacy is also known as the “Flea Theory” (臭虫论): Lu Xun, in his 1933 article “Foreigners Also Have,” satirized how Chinese people, when criticized, would claim that other countries also have the same errors to cover up their own mistakes. “All of China has it; foreign countries have it too. Foreigners say China has fleas, but the West also has fleas.”

Personal Limitation

Literal Translation: Self-Doubt

Due to one’s own level of understanding, one is unable or finds it difficult to comprehend something, and thus concludes that the matter might be wrong or false.

For discussions on certain complex topics, such as “biological evolution and natural selection,” one needs a basic knowledge base on the subject. Simply because one does not know this knowledge, one assumes that these theories must be wrong—this is a fallacy.

Example: Xiao Ming draws a fish and a human, and dismissively asks Xiao Qiang: “Look at these two creatures. Do you really think I would be stupid enough to believe that a fish can randomly transform into a human over time?”

Selective Exception (or Cherry Picking)

When a certain viewpoint is proven to be wrong, one changes the rules of discussion or uses a special exception to excuse the error.

Foolish humans are always reluctant to admit they are wrong. They are not only unwilling to improve their understanding of the problem through better comprehension, but sometimes they stubbornly try to find ways to prove their own correctness. The common method is to find a rationalizing reason for their error after the fact. It is easy to find a reason to believe in what we are accustomed to, but the real difficulty lies in how we test our own worldview after others have confirmed our error, and how we correct our thoughts.

Example: Xiao Ming claims he can predict the future. When everyone tests his predictions in a reasonable scientific environment, he retreats. Xiao Ming says you must first believe that he has precognitive ability before you can see his predictions come true.

Presupposition Questioning (or Leading Question)

Also called “Inductive Questioning,” this involves pre-inserting an assumption into a question, making it so that the respondent, no matter how they answer, appears to be in the wrong.

Presupposition questioning is particularly effective in undermining rational debate because it is provocative. The respondent is often forced to panic and defend themselves.

For example: Xiao Mei and Xiao Li both like Ah Hui. One time, while Ah Hui was present, Xiao Mei deliberately asked Xiao Li in a curious tone: “Xiao Li, have you stopped gambling now?” (The question presupposes that Xiao Li used to gamble.)

Burden of Proof

Assuming that the responsibility of providing evidence lies not with the person proposing the view, but with the person questioning the view.

The person who makes the claim must provide the evidence; the responsibility should not be thrown onto the person who doubts the argument. Just because a view cannot be falsified or no counterexample can be presented does not automatically prove that the view is reasonable or credible. At the same time, we must clearly understand that “nothing is absolute,” so we need to strengthen the credibility of the argument based on known evidence. Dismissing a view simply because it hasn’t been proven is also a fallacy of inference.

Example: Xiao Qiang says he can see ghosts. Just because other people cannot see ghosts does not prove whether his statement is true or not.

Double Entendre

Using a statement with a double meaning or an ambiguous statement that contains ambiguity to mislead or distort the facts.

Politicians often utilize ambiguous statements, and when they are exposed, they point out that, theoretically, what they said was not entirely a lie. But in essence, these statements are misleading from the very beginning.

Example: Zhuang asks A Cong: “You always say you’ll treat me to a meal. When can you fulfill that promise?” A Cong replies: “I’ll go buy you a packet of instant noodles in a bit.”

Gambler’s Fallacy

Believing that there are predictable patterns in independent, random events.

It is like the winning rate of a roulette wheel. Generally speaking, the probability of a single repeated result occurring is extremely low, and the location of the ball each time is completely unrelated to the previous time. For instance, although there is a tiny possibility of twenty consecutive coin flips all landing on heads, the probability of each individual flip landing on heads is still 50/50, and this probability is not affected by the previous flips.

Example: When rolling dice, six consecutive “Big” numbers appear. Zhuang believes that the next roll must definitely be “Small.” As a result, he loses everything.

Blind Conformity (or Bandwagon Effect)

Literal Translation: Bandwagon

Believing that something is correct simply because many people are doing it or agreeing with it.

The fallacy of this viewpoint lies in the fact that the popularity or acceptance of something is completely unrelated to whether it is right or wrong. If we decide right or wrong based on public acceptance, then in the era when people believed the Earth was flat, the Earth should have been flat.

Example: Drunken Old Wang points to Old Zhang and says: “If monsters are just foolish superstitions, why do so many people still believe they truly exist?”

Note: The original English term for this fallacy, “bandwagon,” generally refers to the magnificent carriage carrying a band in a circus parade, and the derived meaning is “a trend or fashion accepted by the public.”

Appeal to Authority

The belief that what an authority figure says must be correct.

It is important to remember that this fallacy does not mean that the claims of a reasonable expert or scientific consensus are unimportant; rather, it means that appealing to authority is not a valid form of argumentation, and the authority’s opinion can also be completely wrong. Therefore, whether someone is an authority or not has no essential impact on whether their claim is true. However, unless a person has a level of understanding or empirical evidence similar to that of an expert, it is unreasonable to disregard the statement of someone with deep knowledge.

Example: Old Zhang doesn’t know how to defend his position that evolution “is not real,” so he says: “I know a famous scientist, Zhuang Zhuang, who also questions evolution!” In fact, Zhuang Zhuang is just a successful fitness coach.

Hasty Generalization

Literal Translation: Combination Division (or Part-to-Whole)

Assuming that a local characteristic of something is the overall characteristic of that thing, or that it applies to other parts of that thing; or that the overall characteristic of an object must apply to each of its independent parts.

This fallacy is also called the “Fallacy of Composition/Division.” Usually, when something is correct for a part, it is indeed possible that it applies to the whole, and vice versa—like saying, “Peeking through a tube, one can see a glimpse.” But the key point is whether there is effective evidence to show that the situation is indeed like that. Simply observing certain consistencies in something may lead to biased thinking, causing us to assume that the consistency exists where it actually does not.

Example: Xiao Cong is a precocious child with logical thinking. He knows that atoms, which are invisible to the naked eye, make up him, so he concludes that he cannot be seen. Unfortunately, despite his thoughts, he still lost the game of hide-and-seek.

Purifying the Argument (or Moving the Goalposts)

Literal Translation: Not a True Scotsman

It is the act of adding premises after the fact, constantly modifying or “purifying” the argument, to refute criticism of your argument’s flaws.

In this form of faulty reasoning, no matter how convincing the evidence is for someone’s belief, simply by changing the standard, the evidence can be made inapplicable to the fabricated so-called “true” example. This post-hoc rationalization is a way of avoiding reasonable criticism of one’s own argument.

Example: A Liang says that Cantonese people only eat sweet tofu pudding. A Hui says that he is Cantonese, but he eats savory tofu pudding. A Liang gets particularly angry and tells A Hui: “True Cantonese people only eat sweet tofu pudding!”

Note: The original English term for this fallacy is “no true Scotsman,” meaning “not a true Scotsman.” It comes from the work On Thinking by Professor Anthony Flew, published in 1975, where he cited a Scotsman who, in order to deny that Scotsmen commit serious crimes, said, “No true Scotsman would do such a thing.”

Genetic Determinism (or Origin Determinism)

Literal Translation: Gene Determines

Judging the good or bad, right or wrong of something based on its origin or the person who proposed the viewpoint.

Also called genetic determinism: Good people and bad people are predetermined in their genes, such as, “You are inherently a bad person, so you are destined only to do bad things and never do good things.” It attempts to evade positive debate by focusing on the origin of a person or thing. Similar to the “Ad Hominem” fallacy, it attacks and discredits the opponent’s viewpoint by utilizing known negative perceptions, yet it doesn’t actually explain what is wrong with the opponent’s argument.

Example: A news channel plays a seismic alert message. Xiao Liang comforts Xiao Hong, saying, “We all know that the news channel, besides celebrity gossip, never broadcasts serious news.”

False Dichotomy (or Black or White)

Only offering two options as choices, while completely ignoring the existence of other possibilities.

Also called “either/or,” “dilemma reasoning,” or “false reasoning.” This insidious strategy superficially presents a logical argument, but upon closer inspection, one can find that there are many more possibilities than the binary choices presented. The binary, black-or-white mindset does not allow for the existence of various variables, conditions, and contexts beyond two possibilities. It only misleads the argument and blocks rational, honest debate.

Example: The Supreme Commander says: “Anyone who doesn’t support his grand blueprint of ‘Making America Great Again’ is an enemy of America.”

Circular Reasoning

The premise of the argument already contains the conclusion.

Such self-contained logic is usually rooted in deep-seated, obsessive assumptions. For example, the cliché: “The main reason circular reasoning is bad is because it is bad.”

Example: The Bullshit Journal is flawless. We know this because The Bullshit Journal itself once stated: “Everything in The Bullshit Journal is true and beautiful; you must not have any doubts.”

Appeal to Nature

Simply because something is “natural” or “of nature,” one assumes it is perfect, and its rationality and effectiveness are indisputable.

Many naturally occurring things are considered beneficial, which may cause our cognition to become biased. Nature itself does not make things good or bad. For example, killing in nature can be seen as very “natural,” but this does not mean that killing is beneficial or rational.

Example: Zhuang believes in “natural remedies,” so when he has a cold or fever, he only drinks plain boiled water, and when he is sick, he only eats herbs. Because he believes that plain boiled water or herbs are more natural than chemically synthesized drugs, they must be more beneficial.

Anecdotal Evidence (or Hearsay)

Using personal experience or isolated cases to replace irrefutable evidence or sound arguments.

People are usually more inclined to believe the statements of others than to understand complex data and changes as a whole. Quantitative scientific measurement is almost always more accurate than personal perception and experience, but we tend to believe things that are tangibly present to us, and what people we trust say, rather than the reality shown by what looks more “abstract” statistics.

Example: Xiao Jie’s grandfather smokes 30 cigarettes a day and still lives to 97 years old. Therefore, Xiao Jie concludes that the research findings proving a causal relationship between smoking and lung cancer cannot be trusted.

Causal Displacement (or Post Hoc Ergo Propter Hoc)

Literal Translation: Texas Sharpshooter

Only selecting evidence that favors oneself or matches one’s own hypothesis.

Although shooting first and then drawing a target center on the bullet hole makes the shooter look like a sharpshooter, there is no necessary causal relationship between the bullet hitting the bullseye and the shooter being a sharpshooter.

Example: Coca-Cola claims that research shows that in the five countries where Coca-Cola sells the most, three countries are among the top ten globally for average IQ. Therefore, drinking Coca-Cola can improve IQ.

Note: The original English term for this fallacy is “the Texas sharpshooter,” referring to a Texas shooter who shoots first and then draws a target.

Middle Ground (or Compromise)

The compromise, or middle ground, between two extremes must certainly be the location of the truth.

Often, the truth does lie between two extreme points, but this can also cause us to develop a cognitive bias: sometimes something is fundamentally wrong, even if it is a compromise. The middle ground between truth and fallacy is still a fallacy.

Example: Xiao Li firmly believes that vaccination causes autism in children, but A Cong, her friend who likes research, says that this claim has been scientifically proven to be false. Then their friend Xiao Mei proposes a compromise argument: Vaccination inevitably causes certain types of autism, not all types of autism.

item.title: When I get that thing, I'll be happy?
item.description: For example, I bought a new car, and now I am waiting to pick it up. Naturally, I pay close attention to this matter, checking and researching related information on forums every evening. Why do I do this? It is just an ordinary car; it won’t bring any substantial change to my life. I know that once I get the car, I won’t pay attention to it anymore. The key issue is my obsession with the “desire” for external objects. The attachment I have towards external things that promise me happiness and joy is actually a form of infatuation.

item.title: Jealousy is the enemy of happiness
item.description: I think that life itself isn’t that difficult; it is ourselves who makes life difficult. I am striving to shed the word “should” in my life. When “should” appears in my mind, what lies behind it is guilt or social conditioning. If you do something because of “should,” it means that your inner self doesn’t want to do it, and going against your own will makes you unbearably miserable. Therefore, I am trying hard to reduce the things I do because of “should” in my life.

item.title: Life is lonely
item.description: The reality is, life is a single-player game. A person is born alone, dies alone, and interprets everything in the world alone. Your memories belong only to you. Before you are born, no one cares; after you leave the world, no one cares. You exist in the world for only a few short decades; life is a single-player game.

item.title: Courage isn't charging into battle amidst heavy gunfire, but rather not caring what others think.
item.description: Don’t spend your time trying to please others. Whether others are happy or not is their problem, not yours.
item.content:encoded: Don’t spend your time trying to please others. Whether others are happy or not is their problem, not yours.

item.title: Possessing independence
item.description: Being responsible for your unique output (rather than being responsible for the time invested, like an employee), this is the most ideal state.
item.content:encoded: Being responsible for your unique output (rather than being responsible for the time invested, like an employee), this is the most ideal state.

item.title: Being carefree is easy, and going with the flow is also easy.
item.description: Extremely smart individuals are often unconventional. They insist on independent thinking and hands-on involvement to clarify the full context of matters.
item.content:encoded: Extremely smart individuals are often unconventional. They insist on independent thinking and hands-on involvement to clarify the full context of matters.

item.title: If you stay away from risks, you will also stay away from the benefits.
item.description: I took a risk. Same with crypto. Early on, I took a risk. But when you put your name out there, you take a risk with certain things. You also get to reap the rewards. You get the benefits.
item.content:encoded: I took a risk. Same with crypto. Early on, I took a risk. But when you put your name out there, you take a risk with certain things. You also get to reap the rewards. You get the benefits.

item.title: People seem to think you can create wealth—make money through work. It’s probably not going to work.
item.description: Without ownership, your inputs are very closely tied to your outputs. In almost any salaried job, even one paying a lot per hour like a lawyer or a doctor, you’re still putting in the hours, and every hour you get paid.
item.content:encoded: Without ownership, your inputs are very closely tied to your outputs. In almost any salaried job, even one paying a lot per hour like a lawyer or a doctor, you’re still putting in the hours, and every hour you get paid.

item.title: Let’s go to the stock market!
item.description: Owning equity in a company basically means you own the upside. When you own debt, you own guaranteed revenue streams and you own the downside. You want to own equity. If you don’t own equity in a business, your odds of making money are very slim.

item.title: Working hard can't make you rich, you can only make your boss rich.
item.description: Your boss will always pay you just good enough.
item.content:encoded: Your boss will always pay you just good enough.

item.title: Don't work for the boss. You must be your own boss.
item.description: Essentially, you’re working for somebody else, and that person is taking on the risk and has the accountability, the intellectual property, and the brand. They’re not going to pay you enough. They’re going to pay you the bare minimum they have to, to get you to do their job. That can be a high bare minimum, but it’s still not going to be true wealth where you’re retired but still earning.

item.title: Nature's law is that you sow in spring and reap in autumn; very few things happen overnight.
item.description: The investment of time is necessary, so I believe that what you need to do is possess expertise, have a sense of responsibility, have influence, utilize the leverage effect, acquire a world-class skill set, and be the best in your professional field.
item.content:encoded: The investment of time is necessary, so I believe that what you need to do is possess expertise, have a sense of responsibility, have influence, utilize the leverage effect, acquire a world-class skill set, and be the best in your professional field.

item.title: No equity, no path to financial freedom.
item.description: If one does not hold corporate equity, the correlation between personal investment and returns will be very strong. For almost all salaried jobs, even high-paying professions like lawyers or doctors, time must be invested to earn the corresponding income. If you don’t hold corporate equity, you have no income while sleeping, no income after retirement, and no income during vacation. In short, the income is relatively fixed, and a substantial breakthrough is fundamentally impossible.

item.title: Utility-driven
item.description: The smaller the desire for something, the fewer the worries, and the less the obsession, which conversely makes one more likely to go with the flow and follow their inner self. You will continue doing it in the way you are skilled at, steadfastly, and the quality of your work will improve as a result.

item.title: The internet has massively broadened the possible space of careers. Most people haven’t figured this out yet.
item.description: You can go on the internet, and you can find your audience. And you can build a business, and create a product, and build wealth, and make people happy just uniquely expressing yourself through the internet.
item.content:encoded: You can go on the internet, and you can find your audience. And you can build a business, and create a product, and build wealth, and make people happy just uniquely expressing yourself through the internet.

item.title: Specific knowledge cannot be taught, but it can be learned.
item.description: You have to do it by yourself.
item.content:encoded: You have to do it by yourself.

item.title: Thinking is too difficult for them, they only need standard answers.
item.description: This is the result of being educated by standard answers since childhood. When the professor discussed the coward’s game, there were clearly already formulas and mathematics available, but they still dare not think about whether or not they can ease gun control.

item.title: "Trying" is purely an excuse
item.description: Even before doing it, the exit strategy has already been planned. Usually, you can’t experiment; you only have two choices—do it or don’t do it. If you approach things with a “just trying it out” mindset, it will most likely end in failure.

item.title: Hard work is important, but there are some things that are more important than hard work
item.description: Work as hard as you can. Even though who you work with and what you work on are more important than how hard you work.

item.title: Don’t look for a get-rich-quick path
item.description: The article debunks get-rich-quick schemes, highlighting how they often benefit the promoters rather than the participants.
item.content:encoded: There are no get-rich-quick schemes. Those are just someone else getting rich off you.

item.title: What’s the difference between wealth and money?
item.description: Money is how we transfer wealth. Money is social credits. It is the ability to have credits and debits of other people’s time.
item.content:encoded: Money is how we transfer wealth. Money is social credits. It is the ability to have credits and debits of other people’s time.

item.title: Smart Pig Game
item.description: This is a game of free-riding, where one party pays the corresponding cost, and both parties share the resulting benefits. Whether individual rationality conflicts with collective rationality depends on the game’s rules. When A < 10, the collective should press (contribute). However, due to unequal income distribution, individuals are unwilling to press (contribute). To resolve this conflict, we should not deny individual interests (let the big pig press selflessly), but rather change the game’s rules (if the small pig doesn’t press, they eat a little less). Therefore, while free-riding, don’t forget to give the other party a return. The wealthy’s willingness to be benevolent depends on the poor person’s endorsement.

item.description: There is a clear lure. The path to the lure is one-way; you can enter but cannot exit (sunk cost). The harder you try to break free, the deeper you fall.

item.title: How to escape the $10,000 trap?
item.description:
People who fall into traps usually have two motivations:

One is the economic motivation, which is a rational motivation—the desire to minimize financial losses. The other is the non-economic motivation: the desire to regain face and punish the opponent.

There are many such traps in life:

For example, two deputy directors want to be promoted and compete by giving gifts. The gifts already given are sunk costs, which cannot be recovered unless you, as the deputy director, decide you don’t want to do it anymore. Another example is the game Zheng Tu (征途): This is a game that changed the landscape of online gaming. In an era where everything required clicking a card, it was permanently free to operate. When you try it for free for a while, you are quickly drawn into the game world. However, you gradually realize that if you don’t pay, you aren’t really playing the game—you are being played by the game. Those “RMB players” who possess various luxurious equipment and high levels will crush you to the point of misery, making you feel your self-esteem has been completely trampled. So, you angrily shout, “Isn’t it because of the RMB? I have it too!” and immediately purchase the full set of luxurious equipment, instantly leveling up, thereby completely defeating the previous defeat and achieving a triumphant return.

But is that all? Of course not. You feel satisfied, so the person who defeated you feels unsatisfied, and thus, you both fall into the trap.

By making people crave the recovery of face, they encourage infinite spending (or “氪金” - kè jīn, i.e., paying to spend/grind) to win back that face. Ultimately, this achieves the goal of sending money to the company.

However, if you own corporate shares, you can receive passive income—meaning the company continues to make money for you even when you are on vacation.

Fundamentally, working a job means working for someone else. Meanwhile, corporate owners possess intellectual property and brand value while also bearing the risk and responsibility. Therefore, the compensation they pay you is always less than the value you create. To get you to work, they will provide you with the minimum necessary compensation.

item.title: There are three types of leverage
item.description: The first type is labor leverage, which means having others work for you. Labor leverage is one of the oldest forms of leverage, but in modern society, its effectiveness is not the best. [1] I even think it is the most outdated form of leverage. This is because managing other people is a very complex and challenging job that requires superb leadership skills. If done poorly, the manager might end up ostracized and devoured by their subordinates.
item.content:encoded:
The first type is labor leverage, which means having others work for you. Labor leverage is one of the oldest forms of leverage, but in modern society, its effectiveness is not the best. [1] I even think it is the most outdated form of leverage. This is because managing other people is a very complex and challenging job that requires superb leadership skills. If done poorly, the manager might end up ostracized and devoured by their subordinates.

Capital is the second, relatively better form of leverage. Capital leverage means using money to expand the influence of decisions. [1] Capital is a more modern form of leverage, and utilizing capital leverage is somewhat difficult, requiring a certain skill set. In the 20th century, people achieved astonishing wealth by utilizing capital leverage. Capital leverage was the primary form of leverage in the 20th century. If you look at the wealthiest people, you will find that the richest are bankers and politicians in corrupt countries—they are essentially all people who can mobilize large amounts of capital. Look at the executives of large companies; besides tech companies, the CEOs of most established large companies are actually doing financial work. The amplifying effect of capital leverage is very obvious. Managing capital is easier than managing people because as capital continuously grows, the difficulty of managing it is far lower than managing an ever-expanding team.

The last type of leverage is the newest and the most accessible to ordinary people. This leverage is “products with zero marginal cost of reproduction.” This includes books, media, movies, and code. Among all leverages that can be used without needing permission from others, code is arguably the most powerful—it only requires a computer.

item.title: How to achieve retirement?
item.description: The article introduced three methods for achieving retirement status: obtaining passive income through saving money, reducing expenses to zero (such as through monastic practice), and engaging in activities one loves without being constrained by money.
item.content:encoded:
Multiple Ways to Achieve Retirement Status

Saving Money

The first method is saving money. As long as the savings are sufficient, passive income (without moving a single finger) can meet your expenses.

Spiritual Practice / Monastic Life

The second method is reducing expenses to zero — through spiritual practice/monastic life.

Doing What You Love

The third method is doing what you love, completely enjoying the process, and not caring whether you have money or not.

In summary, there are many ways to achieve retirement status.

item.title: 省出时间来赚钱才是正确的思路。
Holy Book *Naval Compendium: Guide to Wealth and Happiness*
item.description: Naval Ravikant's profound insights on wealth, knowledge, decision-making, and happiness, helping you build a more successful and fulfilling life.
item.content:encoded:
1. People Should Seek Wealth, Not Money or Status

People should not earn wealth through arduous work. Working 80 hours a week in a restaurant will not make you richer. Hard work is unavoidable, but it should be done in the right way. People should seek wealth, not money or status. If you believe wealth is unimportant, wealth will move away from you. Wealth is assets that continue to make money while you sleep. Without wealth-generating assets, when you sleep, you have no income; when you retire, you cannot keep earning money. In short, without wealth, you cannot achieve non-linear earning. Generally, wealth is created by starting your own company or by investing. Neither of these is achieved by putting in a massive amount of time; the ultra-rich, just like you, only have 24 hours every day.

2. The Key to Acquiring Wealth

To acquire wealth, you can provide something valuable to the masses—especially something they don’t know how to obtain. And you must supply it on a large scale. The internet has greatly expanded career possibilities, and most people still lack a clear understanding of this. Learn marketing, learn creation. If you master these two things, nothing can stop you from succeeding.

3. Arm Yourself with Special Knowledge

Special knowledge is knowledge that cannot be acquired through training. If it can be acquired through training, others can also acquire it, and they can replace you. Special knowledge is usually high in technical sophistication and creative. It cannot be outsourced or automated. (For example, insight) It can be discovered when driven by genuine curiosity and passion. The process of creating special knowledge feels like playing to you, but like working to others. Usually, special knowledge lies at the boundaries of knowledge—things that are either newly understood or genuinely difficult to understand. If you do not commit 100%, someone who commits 100% will surpass you. And they won’t just be slightly better; they will be much better, because in the realm of ideas, compound interest will work, and leverage will work. Special knowledge might be things like: Sales skills. Having musical talent. Persistence: This means you can research things with dedication. Loving science fiction: This means you can quickly absorb a lot of knowledge. Playing many games: This means you have a good understanding of game theory. Gossip: This might help you become a very interesting journalist. Special knowledge is a strange combination, coming from your DNA, your unique environment of growth, and your response to that knowledge. These are almost integrated into your personality and identity, and then you can continuously refine them. Study microeconomics, game theory, psychology, brainwashing techniques, ethics, mathematics, and computer science.

4. Arm Yourself with Leverage

Business leverage mainly consists of capital, labor, and products with extremely low replication costs (code and media). Capital refers to money. To raise funds, you need to use your special knowledge, combined with your sense of responsibility, to demonstrate your good judgment. Labor refers to the people who work for you. It is the oldest and most fiercely contested form of leverage. Labor leverage will make your parents feel proud, but don’t waste your life pursuing this alone. Capital and labor are forms of leverage that require permission to use. Everyone chases capital, but there must always be someone to pay for it. Everyone wants to lead others, but there must always be subordinates. Code and media are forms of leverage that require no permission; they are the leverage behind the new rich. You can create software and media that work for you even while you sleep. A large group of robots is available for free use—to save space and energy efficiency, they are packaged into data centers; use them! By applying special knowledge combined with leverage, you will ultimately get what you deserve.

5. In One Sentence: Productize Yourself

What does this mean? “Productize” and “yourself.” “Yourself” has uniqueness; “productize” has leverage. “Am I productizing it? Can I scale it? Can I amplify it through labor, capital, code, or media?” So, this phrase is very easy to remember. If you want to be richer, you must figure out what you can provide to society that society doesn’t know how to obtain, but that society wants, and providing it to you is natural and within your skill set and capability. Next, you must find a way to scale it, because producing only one is far from enough. You might need to produce thousands, or tens of thousands, or millions, or even billions, so that everyone can have one. Steve Jobs (and his team, of course) figured out that society needed a smartphone. This smartphone had all the functions of phones at the time, but also many other new functions, and it was easier to use. Therefore, they figured out how to manufacture the smartphone, and then they figured out how to mass-produce the smartphone. You must become the person who can scale the provision of these products or services. This is the real challenge of how to make money.

6. Pay Attention to Your Character

In my life, I have known some extremely successful, very popular, and very smart people. However, I have seen them do one or two things that were not very good for others. I would say, “Hey, I think you shouldn’t do this to others. Because it will ultimately hurt yourself.” Deep down, we all know who we are. You cannot hide anything from yourself. You are very clear whether what you do is right or wrong; if you have too many moral flaws, you will not respect yourself. The worst outcome in this world is a lack of self-respect. If you don’t love yourself, who will love you? If I see someone doing this, the first time I will remind them, but usually they won’t change, and then I will keep my distance from them. I cut them out of my life. If someone constantly claims to be honest, they are likely dishonest. These are just some effective indicators that I have learned. When someone spends a lot of time talking about their values or talking about themselves, it means they are hiding something. I think to myself: “If you want to get close to me, your values must be better than mine.”

7. Smart People Truly Understand One Thing

If someone uses many complex words and many grand concepts, they are likely unaware of what they are actually talking about. I believe the smartest people can explain things to a child. If you cannot explain it to a child, then you don’t truly know it. Truly smart thinkers are clear-thinking thinkers; they understand very, very basic foundational knowledge.

8. Step Outside Yourself to See the Truth

Imagine one of my friends is going through some difficulties, such as a breakup, career issues, business failure, or health problems. When he needs my advice, it often takes me only a few minutes to accurately tell him, “Oh, that girl, forget her. Anyway, she’s not good for you. You will be happier. Believe me. You will find someone more suitable in the future.” But he himself finds it difficult to see this. Because he is in pain and torment, his desires conflict with reality, which prevents him from seeing the truth clearly. The same thing happens when we make decisions. To see the truth clearly, you must set aside the self, because the self does not want to face the truth.

9. What is Truly Important is Leisure Time

Great ideas only come after you feel bored. Good ideas never appear when you are under pressure, busy, rushing around, or in a hurry. If your schedule doesn’t have one or two days a week where you aren’t constantly in meetings or constantly busy, you cannot think. You won’t have good ideas related to your business. You also cannot make good judgments. I encourage you to set aside at least one day a week (better yet, two days, because if you prepare two days, you will definitely find one) so that you have time to think. Cherish your time; it is everything. It is more important than your money. It is more important than your friends. It is more important than anything. Your time is everything. Don’t waste your time.

10. Reading Can Make You Successful

Spending one hour a day reading science, mathematics, and philosophy can likely put you on the high ladder of human success within seven years. I have spent a lot of time reading. My only true friend is books. Books are great friends because they tell you the wisdom of the best thinkers over the past thousands of years. Any book that has survived for two thousand years has been screened by many people, and it is more likely to be correct; I want to reread these books. The fact is, I read not for self-improvement. I read out of curiosity and interest. The best book is the one that captivates you.

11. Do Things for Your Own Goals

I truly want to do things for my own goals. Whether it is business, fitness, romance, friendship, or anything else, I believe the meaning of life is to do things for your own goals. When you do things for yourself, you can create your best work. Even if you do these things to make money, you will actually be the most successful. Follow your true curiosity, not the current hot topics. If your curiosity leads you to where society will eventually go, you will receive rich rewards. When you are dating, there is a moment you realize that the relationship will not lead to marriage, you might be better off moving on. When you are learning something, such as geography or history, and you realize you will never use this information, drop that course. That is wasting time. That is wasting mental energy.

12. Become a Better Decision-Maker Overall

Become a better decision-maker overall. Decision-making is everything. Yes. Decision-making is everything. In fact, someone who makes correct decisions 80% of the time instead of 70% of the time will have value and compensation in the market hundreds of times higher. I believe people find it difficult to understand a basic fact of leverage. If I manage $1 billion, and I am often 10% more correct than others, my decisions can bring $100 million in value in a single judgment. With modern technology, massive labor, and capital, the multiplier of our decisions can be leveraged to increasingly higher levels. If I face a difficult choice, such as these questions: Should I marry this person? Should I take this job? Should I buy this house? Should I move to this city? Should I partner with this person in business? If you cannot decide, answer no. The reason is that modern society is full of choices. There are so many choices. We live on a planet with 7 billion people, and we can connect with everyone through the internet. There are hundreds of thousands of professions for you to choose from. There are so many choices. When you choose certain things, you are locked in for a very long time. Starting a business might take 10 years. Starting a relationship might take 5 years or more. Moving to a city might take 10 to 20 years. These are all decisions with very, very long-term impact. We only say “yes” when we are very certain. You can never be absolutely certain, but you must be very confident. If you have two choices, and they are relatively equal, then choose the path that is more difficult and more painful in the short term. The reality is that one path will endure short-term pain. The other path will feel pain further down the line in the future. However, your brain tries to avoid conflict and tries to avoid short-term pain. By definition, if two choices are similar, and one has short-term pain, then this choice is related to long-term gain. According to the law of compound interest, long-term gain is what you want. Your brain overvalues short-term happiness and tries to avoid short-term pain. Caffeine is another thing that trades long-term consequences for short-term benefits. Essentially, you must, through your life, replace bad habits you unconsciously acquire with good habits, committing to become a happier person.

13. On Happiness

Confucius said that a person has two lives, and the second life begins when you realize that life is only one. So, when and how does your second life begin? (Confucius said: I never said that.) I read a quote by Blaise Pascal. It roughly means: “All of humanity’s unhappiness is because they cannot sit quietly in their rooms.” If you sit for 30 minutes and feel happy, you are successful. This is a very high state, but few people achieve it. The core skill you must learn is to be content with circumstances and go with the flow in most situations. You can get almost anything you want from life, as long as it is what you want the most. The first rule of handling conflict is: don’t be with people who frequently cause conflict. I am not interested in things that are not sustainable or difficult to sustain, including relationships full of problems.

14. The Top Priority of Life

The top priority of my life, above my happiness, above my family, above my work, is my own health. First is my physical health. Second is my mental health. Third is my spiritual health. After that, is my family’s health. After that, is my family’s happiness. After that, I can do anything else in the world that I need to do. Basically, whenever you recommend a good habit to someone, they will find an excuse for themselves, and the most common excuse is usually, “I don’t have time.” When you hear this, you know they are saying, “This is not a high-priority matter.” If something is your top priority, you will do it. That is how life works. If you have 10 to 15 vague and non-urgent matters, you will ultimately not do any of them. What I do is decide that the top priority in my life, above my happiness, above my family, above my work, is my health. My physical health has become my top priority, so I can never say I don’t have time. In the morning, I exercise, no matter how long it takes, I insist on exercising. If I haven’t finished exercising, I won’t start the day’s work. I don’t care if the world is collapsing and melting; it can wait another 30 minutes until I finish exercising. Just like other things in life, if you are willing to make short-term sacrifices, you will have long-term benefits. “Easy choice, difficult life. Difficult choice, easy life.”

15. Don’t Fight Your Own Thoughts

Don’t take yourself too seriously. You are just a monkey with a plan. Don’t make any decisions, don’t make any judgments; just accept everything. If I walk and do this for ten to fifteen minutes, I enter a very calm, grateful state. Non-judgmental consciousness is very useful to me. Another method I learned is to sit there, close my eyes, for at least an hour every day. You surrender to whatever happens—without effort. You don’t strive to do certain things, nor do you strive to oppose certain things. If thoughts flow through your mind, you flow with those thoughts. “If a thought comes, a thought comes. I don’t fight it. I don’t embrace it. I don’t think about it. I don’t reject it. I just sit there with my eyes closed for an hour, doing nothing.” This is a state of happiness, bliss, and tranquility. Once you have it, you don’t want to give it up. If you can gain an hour of happy freedom time just by sitting with your eyes closed every morning, that is priceless. It will change your life. All you have to do is sit there and do nothing. Just sit down. Close your eyes and say: “I just want to rest for an hour. This is an hour away from life, an hour where I do nothing.”

16. Let Consciousness and Mind Coexist Harmoniously

Buddhists talk about consciousness and the self; they truly view your brain as a multi-layered mechanism: a core-level operating system is running, and then there are some applications running on top of it. I am returning to the operating system of my consciousness layer, which is always calm, always peaceful, usually happy and satisfied. I try to maintain this state instead of activating the “monkey mind” (referring to the mind below consciousness). The monkey mind is always worried, afraid, and anxious; it has incredible power, but I try not to activate it until I need it. If I run it non-stop for 24 hours, I will waste energy, and the monkey mind will become me; I am more important than my monkey mind. The mind itself is a muscle—it can be trained and regulated, but it has been haphazardly trained by society into a form that we cannot control. If you examine your mind with consciousness and intention, I think you can extract your own thoughts, emotions, ideas, and reactions, and then you can start reprogramming. You can rewrite this program according to your will.

17. How to Define Wisdom?

A person understands the long-term consequences of what they do.

item.title: Why is rich people's money more valuable than ordinary people's money?
item.description:
What? Are Money Values Tiered?

Or is it because they possess some special investment strategy? In this article, we will explore the differences between the money of the rich and the ordinary, and provide some practical suggestions to help ordinary people achieve wealth growth.
item.content:encoded:
What? Are Money Values Tiered?

Does the money of the rich hold more value than the money of the ordinary person? Why is that? Is it because the rich spend money better than the ordinary person? Or is it because they possess some special investment strategy? In this article, we will explore the differences between the money of the rich and the ordinary, and provide some practical suggestions to help ordinary people achieve wealth growth.

The Money of the Rich Has Potential Growth Value

Let’s start with a simple example. Suppose both the rich and the ordinary person have 10,000 yuan. For the ordinary person, this 10,000 yuan might be used for daily expenses, such as clothes, pants, bags, rent, or mortgage payments. Although these expenses are necessary, they do not generate any additional income. In contrast, the rich person’s 10,000 yuan might be invested in stocks, bonds, real estate, etc. While these investments carry a certain risk, they can also bring substantial returns.

For example, suppose the rich person invests 10,000 yuan in a stock with an annualized return rate of 10%. Then, next year, this 10,000 yuan will become 11,000 yuan, and the year after, it will become 12,100 yuan, and so on. This potential growth value makes the rich person’s money more valuable than the ordinary person’s money.

The Rich Spend Money More Prudently

So, why are the rich more cautious when spending money? It is because they need to consider the potential consequences of spending, including the impact on future income. For the rich, spending 10,000 yuan is not just spending 10,000 yuan; it means giving up potential investment returns. Therefore, they consider the necessity and potential consequences of spending more carefully.

For instance, suppose the rich person needs to buy a new car. They might consider factors such as the car’s price, fuel efficiency, maintenance costs, and compare it with other investment opportunities. They might ask themselves:

  • Is this car worth spending so much money on?
  • Are there better investment opportunities?

This cautious attitude makes the rich more rational and prudent in their spending.

Spending Ratio of the Rich vs. Ordinary People

So, what is the difference in the spending ratio between the rich and the ordinary person? According to research, the income of the ordinary person is often entirely used for expenses, while the spending ratio of the rich is extremely low. For example, suppose the ordinary person’s monthly income is 5,000 yuan, and they might use their entire income for expenses, such as rent, mortgage, and living costs. In contrast, the rich person’s monthly income might be 50,000 yuan, but their spending ratio might only be 1%. This means they have more money available for investment and savings.

Conclusion

By exploring the differences between the money of the rich and the ordinary, we found that the rich person’s money is more valuable because it has potential growth value. We also found that the rich are more prudent when spending, because they need to consider the potential consequences of spending. Finally, we learned that there is a significant difference in the spending ratio between the rich and the ordinary.

Recommendations

So, how can ordinary people achieve wealth growth by changing their spending habits and investment strategies? Here are some practical suggestions:

  • Start Investing: Consider using your money for investment. How to invest is another serious topic.
  • Reduce Expenses: Try to reduce your spending ratio, leaving more money for investment and savings.
  • Spend Prudently: When spending, consider the potential consequences of the expenditure, including the impact on future income.

By taking these measures, ordinary people can begin to achieve wealth growth and make their money more valuable.
